Despite its economic significance, no comprehensive solution utilizing advanced digital technologies has been developed specifically for tea plantations in Sri Lanka. This research proposes an integrated smart system that leverages the Internet of Things (IoT), Digital Twins, and carbon footprint tracking to enhance operational efficiency, sustainability, and traceability in tea plantation management. The proposed system comprises four key components: a Portable IoT Device for real-time environmental monitoring, a Digital Twin for Yield Prediction and Harvest Management, a Digital Twin for Data Visualization, and a Product Passport with Carbon Footprint tracking. By utilizing real-time data collection, predictive analytics, and interactive visualization, the system provides actionable insights for optimizing resource usage, scheduling harvests, and minimizing carbon emissions. The research methodology involves designing and implementing each component using advanced tools and technologies, including Python, TensorFlow, Unity, Solidity and C#. This study is the first to explore the application of these technologies in Sri Lankan tea plantations, addressing critical industry challenges while enhancing sustainability and market competitiveness. The findings demonstrate the system's potential to revolutionize tea plantation management by improving productivity, ensuring product authenticity, and promoting environmentally sustainable practices.

title: Enhancing Data Integrity and Authenticity for Blockchain Powered Online Healthcare Services
authors: A. Krishnan; R. Arunachalam
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
abstract: Healthcare fraud in insurance claims imposes substantial financial and operational burdens on healthcare systems, necessitating secure and intelligent detection mechanisms. Existing machine learning and blockchain-based frameworks often lack relational modeling capability, interpretability, or scalable real-time validation within decentralized environments. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Blockchain-Integrated Trust-Aware Graph Attention Learning (TA-GAL) framework for secure and interpretable healthcare fraud detection using the NHIS Healthcare Claims and Fraud Dataset. The model constructs a claim-level relational graph and dynamically adjusts attention weights based on trust propagation, while a permissioned blockchain implemented using Hyperledger Fabric with PBFT consensus ensures tamper-resistant transaction validation. The proposed model was implemented using Python (PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric, and Hyperledger Fabric SDK). Experimental results demonstrate superior performance, achieving 96.84% accuracy, 95.35% F1-score, and 0.982 ROC-AUC, reflecting an approximate 4% improvement over conventional ensemble baselines. The framework effectively enhances transparency, security, and fraud detection reliability, making it suitable for secure, real-world healthcare claim auditing environments.

title: BotNet-Inspired HTTP-Based DDoS Attack Prevention Using Supervised Machine Learning Algorithms in Internet of Things Devices
authors: J. E. Taiwo Akinsola; S. A. Ajagbe; A. O. Lawal; E. A. Olajubu; G. A. Aderounmu; M. O. Adigun
venue: 2024 IEEE International Systems Conference (SysCon)
abstract: DDoS attacks have emerged as the most serious Internet risks, causing significant damage to businesses and governments. This study utilized the BoT-IoT dataset obtained from the University of New South Wales (UNSW) website on machine learning (ML) algorithms to prevent HTTP-based DDoS attacks in the Internet of Things environment. Character encoding was performed to convert the strings such as DDoS attack to 1 and Non-malicious to 0. Feature scaling and normalization were carried out to normalize numerical data with large values using a Python module called standard scaler to avoid model overfitting or underfitting. According to the performance evaluation metrics results, decision tree is the best model with 99.96% accuracy, 0.9979 R2, 0.0003 MAE, 0.0003 MSE, 0.0195 RMSE, 1.0 precision, 0.9994 recall, 0.9997 F1_score after dimensionality reduction. After comparing various ML models, this study concludes that the decision tree is the golden model for HTTP-based DDoS attack prevention in IoT devices. The study recommends the utilization of other performance evaluation metrics such as Matthew Correlation Coefficient (MCC), Kappa Statistic and Huber loss for further studies to avoid bias and subjectivity in the model selection where there are surrogate models. Also, deep learning paradigms can be implemented for the prevention of HTTP-based DDoS attacks in cloud environments.

title: Smart Summarization of Terms & Conditions: Making Legal Jargon User-Friendly
authors: P. Chingunde; N. Ranjan; P. Wattamwar; P. Sawalkar; P. Kadam; P. Bhoyar
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Integration of Computational Intelligent System (ICICIS)
abstract: Generally, legal documents are often skimmed by many individuals because the lengthy content with dense legal jargon makes them complex and inaccessible. Many users usually bypass such texts without reading and risk their privacy. Summarizing text with key words and phrases makes it easier to understand the overall scenario by reading only the essential information. This research accomplishes it by making use of NLP and Machine Learning with algorithms such as PEGASUS and BERT, which provide extractive and abstractive summarization, emphasizing context understanding and content prioritization according to importance. Our new approach integrates Legal-BERT for classifying phrases into different categories, while graphical visualization of the results using Python libraries such as Matplotlib makes the information easier to absorb. Multilingual support using models like mBERT addresses the needs of a global audience. By classifying, prioritizing, visualizing, and summarizing the text, our research helps users make informed and confident decisions, especially for online services or platforms. Unlike prior studies that address summarization or classification in isolation, our framework uniquely integrates abstractive and extractive summarization, clause classification, multilingual processing, risk scoring, and visualization into a unified system. Preliminary evaluation on sample legal documents shows encouraging results, with competitive ROUGE and BLEU scores and improved comprehension in user feedback, making the system a practical step toward enhancing transparency, accessibility, and trust in legal agreements.

title: Meta-agentic Framework for Software bug detection using Large Language Models
authors: S. Padmanabhuni; B. Karuturi; J. K. Indupalli; S. R. Chilla; V. Yelleti
venue: 2026 18th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: Software bugs, whether introduced intentionally or unintentionally, pose critical risks to software reliability, often leading to financial and reputational losses. Traditional deep learning–based approaches such as CNN, LSTM, and transformer models have automated bug detection to some extent but struggle with contextual reasoning, scalability, and handling large software systems. To address these limitations of extant approaches, this study proposes a novel Meta-Agentic Framework for Software Bug Detection that employs multiple Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents working collaboratively. The framework operates in two-stage manner wherein the first stage involves three specialized agents, namely, (i) module-wise, (ii) cross-module, (iii) RAG-based agents. Each one of these agents identifies bugs from an unique perspective and then all the identified bugs and recommended codes are then passed on to (iv) meta-agent, which cross-verifies and filters out hallucinated or redundant bugs to ensure accuracy in a collaborative manner. A FAISS vector database supports the retrieval-augmented detector by identifying structurally similar bugs from historical data. The framework was evaluated on 55 real-world Python programs, including Pandas, SpaCy, Keras, Matplotlib, and FastAPI. The proposed agentic framework turned out to be the winner in 22 total wins, followed by module-wise (14), RAG-based (10), and cross-module (9) agents. Further, the mean Levenshtein distance turned out to be lower (553.85) for the proposed agentic framework than for any single agent, thereby indicating a higher quality of the recommended codes. Overall, the proposed meta-agentic LLM framework provides a scalable, context-aware, and trustworthy approach to intelligent software debugging, outperforming traditional single-agent systems.

title: Designing Secure Clusters using Blockchain for IoT
authors: B. Karthik; S. G. G H; M. N S; S. C. Swamy
venue: 2022 IEEE 7th International conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Internet of Things(IoT) has become a major component of our lives, where numerous independent devices connect, communicate and interact with one another. It is an evolving technology where devices are intelligent, independent and exchange information with one another without the need for human intervention. Hence these devices must identify, authenticate each other and ensure data integrity and security to avoid being targeted by various malicious attacks. To overcome these limits, a secure decentralized system has been proposed in this work. Here devices can create secure clusters along with security features provided by blockchains, where devices can identify, authenticate and trust each other for data integrity and availability. The implementation of proposed work is done using java and python language and also using ethereum blockchain. Initially, there was only one mode of communication where devices belonging to the same cluster could communicate with each other which are termed as Intra cluster communication. In the proposed system, major focus is on the Inter cluster communication where devices belonging to different clusters can communicate with each other. By using inter cluster communication, the performance and availability of data for the application are enhanced. The results obtained in the proposed work will satisfy the security, efficiency, and low cost needs of the Internet of Things.

title: Carbon Footprint Minimization in 5G Networks Using Blockchain Integrated Renewable Energy Management Framework
authors: M. DSouza; S. B.L; S. S; R. P. Landage; S. G; M. Karthik
venue: 2025 IEEE Pune Section International Conference (PuneCon)
abstract: The rapid growth of 5G networks has created a huge upsurge in energy consumption, raising severe issues regarding carbon emissions and sustainability. Although current strategies like energy-efficient routing, smart grid optimization, and renewable energy integration have tried to counter these impacts, they suffer from a lack of real-time optimization and decentralized control, leading to inefficient carbon reduction and unacceptable energy cost efficiency. In order to fill these gaps, this study presents a novel framework known as BAREO-LP (Blockchain-Assisted Renewable Energy Optimization using Linear Programming) which incorporates blockchain-based peer-to-peer energy trading, renewable energy (solar and battery) modeling, and an emission-conscious linear programming optimization framework. The developed model is utilized through the Python programming language and evaluated on the publicly available 5G-Energy Consumption Dataset from Kaggle. Experimental outcomes show a 58% decrease in carbon emissions and a 32% cost reduction against conventional grid-based and smart grid scenarios. The method also gains an accuracy gain of 16% in energy demand forecasting with minimized load balancing and resource optimization. The blockchain module provides trust and transparency in peer-to-peer energy trading, making the model scalable and realizable in real-world 5G implementations. This multi-faceted strategy sets a new standard for green communication infrastructures and calls for further investigation in sustainable 5G network planning.

title: Demystifying Complexity: A Component-Based Approach to Democratizing Domain Workflows
authors: G. Oyeyemi; M. Ali; C. Hoare; S. Coffee; T. Margaria; J. O'Donnell
venue: 2026 IEEE 50th Annual Computers, Software, and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
abstract: Modern engineering workflows, especially in complex fields like energy modelling, are often limited by rigid, monolithic scripting. Dependence on ad-hoc “semi-structured code” isolates critical intellectual property, increases technical debt, and restricts scalability. We introduce a component-based approach that refactors legacy scripts into reusable Service Independent Building Blocks (SIBs). Using a national housing archetype pipeline for energy consumption prediction as a case study, we present a three-phase framework for the approach: Identification, Abstraction, and Definition. This process converts static Python code into dynamic, governed assets. We show how this shift enables domain experts to become Citizen Engineers, supporting rapid scenario modelling and software application development. This also improves data governance, and fosters rapid innovation in a secure Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) environment.

title: Next-Generation Communication and Computing Frameworks for Smart Cities
authors: P. G. Sonar; D. Ranoji; S. B. Shaikh; S. Y. Kulkarni; N. G. Deshmukh; V. R. Parihar
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Multimedia, Signal Processing and Communication Technologies (IMPACT)
abstract: This paper presents a Next-Generation Communication and Computing Framework (NG-CCF) that integrates adaptive connectivity, distributed intelligence and blockchain enabled trust for smart city environments. The framework provides a unified framework that incorporates four layers that are interdependent such as device, edge/fog, blockchain coordination, and cloud orchestration to optimize both communication and computation resources jointly. Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents deployed at the edge dynamically balance task offloading and local execution, whereas a blockchain layer ensures verifiable data exchange and secure coordination among distributed entities. A mixed simulation environment was created based on OMNeT++, RL written in Python, and Hyperledger Fabric to test the system performance in case of realistic dynamic loads. The findings show that NG-CCF reduces the latency by about 26%, decreases the energy consumption by 22%, and attains a trust index of 0.97 when compared to the baseline models. These results refer to the fact that a smart integration between communication and computation can provide efficiency and reliability when it comes to large-scale urban deployments. The suggested model offers a universal roadmap to autonomous, secure and energy-aware smart urban ecosystems that can support next-generation 6G connectivity and real-time analytics.

title: Towards Decentralized Governance in Microgrids: A DAO-Based Framework
authors: N. R. Naraindath; R. M. Naidoo; R. C. Bansal
venue: 2026 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power Electronics & IoT Applications in Renewable Energy and its Control (PARC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) framework for microgrid governance, specifically targeting diverse stakeholder ownership. It integrates principles of decentralization, democratization, and digitization to streamline the just energy transition. The multifaceted model synthesizes key DAO mechanisms with microgrid elements by incorporating tokenomics, fund management, actor reputation, decision-making, tender selections and dispute resolutions. Preliminary conceptual validation in Python case studies demonstrates the feasibility of the approach. However, further research and validation are needed to pave the way from centralized structures to a more empowered, equitable and resilient future.

title: ReForge: A Customizable AI-Driven Framework for End-to-End Exploit Generation and Analysis
authors: S. S. Prabhakar; D. Gammanpilage; A. Harsha; M. Sudhakar; S. B. Bhat; T. Banerjee
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Future Machine Learning and Data Science (FMLDS)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce ReForge, a novel, end-to-end AI-based software framework for detecting vulnerabilities in code and automatically generating exploits that trigger these vulnerabilities. Traditional manual approaches to vulnerability detection and exploit generation are time-consuming and struggle to keep pace with the rapid evolution of code. ReForge implements an iterative feedback loop over an MCP server to ensure reliability in exploit generation. Its modular architecture enables seamless future extensions. In under one minute, ReForge generated working Python exploits for all evaluated C/C++ targets, achieving up to a 168x speedup over beginner analysts, while maintaining high token efficiency and low overall token cost. This democratizes advanced exploit development and lays the groundwork for flexible automated security workflows.

title: Blockchain-Enabled Cybersecurity for Renewable Energy Systems: Architecture and Performance Evaluation
authors: A. -S. T. Hussain; A. H. A. -D. Ahmed; M. M. Salman; A. H. A. Wahhab; A. G. Ibraheem; A. M. Hussein; F. A. Abdulsalam; T. M. Al-Naimi; T. Almulaisi
venue: 2026 2nd International Symposium on AI-Driven Engineering Systems (ISADES)
abstract: Incorporation of renewable energy sources (RES), such as photovoltaic (PV), wind and battery storage systems, into today’s smart grid has increased the attack surface for the cyber adversary. The geographically distributed, heterogeneous and resource-limited nature of energy devices means that conventional, centralized security models are inadequate to provide the necessary trust, transparency and tamper resistance. This paper proposes a cybersecurity architecture for renewable energy systems by combining a 5-layer framework including edge devices, network gateways, permissioned distributed ledger, and a machine-learning-based intrusion detection unit, which is enabled by blockchain. Every transaction from smart inverters and meters is authenticated with Elliptic-Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) signatures and hashing using SHA-256 to balance the security requirements with the low latency requirement of the grid telemetry. A Python-3.11 prototype is used to evaluate the framework with six types of attacks: Denial of Service (DoS), Man-in-the-Middle (MITM), False Data Injection (FDI), Replay, Sybil, and Data Injection, for networks of different sizes (5 to 160 nodes). The experiments were performed on an Intel Core i7 workstation (16 GB RAM, Ubuntu 22.04), repeated 30 times, and with $95 \%$ confidence intervals. The results show that the proposed PoA-based framework can obtain the average detection accuracy of $96.1 \%$, the AUC of 0.972, the maximum throughput of more than 800 transactions per second (tx/s), the end-to-end latency of less than 20 milliseconds (ms) at $\mathbf{5 0 0 ~ t x} \boldsymbol{/} \mathbf{s}$, and the CPU utilization of only 28% on edge nodes.

title: KONSTRAKT-An AI-Powered Job and Project Networking Platform for the Philippine Construction Industry Using TF-IDF and Cosine Similarity Matching
authors: J. M. A. Valdoria; A. Caballero; A. F. Medina
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The Philippine construction industry, despite being a key economic driver, faces persistent productivity challenges stemming from a severe skills mismatch and dependence on fragmented, informal recruitment networks. Approximately 80% of the sector's workforce operates informally, with an estimated 65–70% of local hiring conducted through word-of-mouth and the traditional "standby" system, where workers physically gather at street corners awaiting daily wage opportunities. These inefficiencies result in underemployment among skilled workers and recurring project delays for contractors, largely due to the absence of a centralized, credentialverified hiring channel. This study developed KONSTRAKT, a mobile and web-based job networking platform designed to professionalize construction recruitment in Metro Manila. Built on React Native for cross-platform accessibility and Supabase for a secure, scalable backend, the platform's core innovation is an AIpowered matching engine developed using Python and scikit-learn. The engine applies Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) and Cosine Similarity algorithms to structured user profiles, prioritizing verifiable TESDA certifications, technical skills, and geolocation data to generate accurate worker-to-project compatibility scores. By transitioning the industry from informal recruitment practices to a data-driven digital marketplace with verifiable credentials, KONSTRAKT reduces search friction, increases workforce visibility, and bridges the trust gap between workers and contractors. The platform advances inclusive economic growth aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure).

title: Characterizing the Growth of a Laser-Induced Air Plasma Using a High-Speed Camera
authors: M. Zhang; L. VanHouten; H. Hasson; P. . -A. Gourdain
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Plasma Science (ICOPS)
abstract: The prominence of high-powered lasers in research, aerodynamics, and manufacturing makes understanding laser-driven air breakdown important to the diagnosis of issues in expensive laser systems. We measure the expansion speed of a laser-induced plasma plume by focusing a 532 nm, 1 ns, 1 J laser pulse with a lens to cause breakdown in air at atmospheric pressure. We then recorded the plasma plume's evolution using a 1 GHz camera and analyzed the resulting images with Python. 19 shots displaying plasma growth were collected. The laser sparks propagated back towards the laser source at speeds up to 400 km/s within 3 ns of their formation, then continued growing at slower speeds until the laser sparks reached their maximum width at around 5 mm. The plasma displayed beading during the fading stage, and then contracted until no longer visible. Further investigation will involve examining the patterns and causes of the observed beading and determining the factors behind the irregular, rapid increases in plasma growth and width over time.

title: Development of a Functional Testing System for Test Automation and Statistical Analysis of the behavior of health care device used to treat Deep Vein Thrombosis
authors: D. M. P.; R. Shivram
venue: 2018 3rd IEEE International Conference on Recent Trends in Electronics, Information & Communication Technology (RTEICT)
abstract: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) is a health condition caused by a blood clot formed in a vein lying deep below the skin. It is treated by increasing the venous blood flow in the affected limb. The DVT health care device achieves this by mimicking the body's natural muscle contractions using a pressure controlled air bag placed on the affected limb. Functional testing of such portable devices is important to detect any deviations from the intended behavior and to collect data for statistical analysis. In this study, a functional testing system is developed to extensively test a DVT health care device and collect data for statistical analysis to predict its behaviour. The testing requires simulating a certain sequence of the end user's actions, which is automated by the testing system. The test is initiated using a mobile app which communicates with the testing system using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). The testing system then starts the DVT device, feeds in different pressure values through BLE communication and observes its behavior by collecting pressure sensor readings at various time intervals. Based on the medically acceptable range for peak and stabilized pressure values, the test is declared as successful. The test results for all the DVT devices are communicated to the mobile app. This test automation considerably reduces the time and effort to test all the manufactured DVT devices. Data analysis tools are used to perform descriptive statistical analysis that provides a summary of the collected data and its visualization. Inferential statistical analysis is performed to estimate the behavior of the manufactured DVT devices during long operational hours. The inferences are validated by performing parametric statistical tests on the collected data. Statistical data analysis is done using Python.

title: Prediction of Bontang City COVID-19 Data Time Series Using the Facebook Prophet Method
authors: K. Kasturi; M. I. A. Putera; S. R. Natasia
venue: 2021 4th International Seminar on Research of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ISRITI)
abstract: The increasing trend of COVID-19 cases in Bontang makes it the first order of the highest incident rate in East Kalimantan, with a value of 1161.78 cases per 100 thousand inhabitants. The purpose of this study was to predict the increase in COVID-19 cases in Bontang City with a data set of positive confirmed cases, recovered and died of COVID-19 in Bontang city. The data set used starts from March 24, 2020 - March 1, 2021, using the Facebook Prophet method, the Jupyter Notebook application, and the Python programming language. The research process consists of the data collection stage, prediction implementation stage (data preprocessing, processing, performance evaluation, dashboard creation), and analysis of the result. The prediction was performed for up to 92 days until May 5, 2021. The result shows a trend of increasing cases of covid reaching the highest positive value, the highest recovery, and highest death, respectively, of 8695, 6099, and 156 people. According to the model, the average positive predictive error (MAE) and the average positive predictive accuracy value (MAPE) are 0.17 and 17.4%, indicating the positive prediction of contracting covid has good accuracy criteria. The next evaluation for the death prediction is accounted as reasonable accuracy criteria in which MAE and MAPE are 0.27 and 27%, respectively. Lastly, the recovery prediction has MAE of 0.17 and MAPE of 17.4%, implying good accuracy criteria. The study also provides recommendations to the COVID-19 Task Force to prepare the minimum number of PCR Tests by 870 tests and increase the hospitalization occupancy by 294 to control the spreading of the Coronavirus.

title: Validation of an algorithm for automatic calculation of inter-lesion distance in radiofrequency catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation
authors: F. Setién-Dodero; F. Fanjul-Vélez; J. L. Arce-Diego
venue: 2024 46th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
abstract: Atrial Fibrillation (AF) is a heart rhythm disorder characterized by rapid and irregular atrial contractions, which can increase the risk of stroke and decrease patients' quality of life. One of the main techniques to treat AF is RF catheter ablation, which involves electrically isolating the pulmonary veins from the rest of the atrium, based on point lesions surrounding the veins. There is still discussion in the community as to what is the optimal interlesion distance to improve the long-term results of AF ablation. A Python tool has been developed that, starting from the AF ablation procedure data, finds the optimal sequence of ablations surrounding the pulmonary veins and thus can calculate the distance between the entire sequence of lesions. The automated algorithm proved to be effective in most cases and in almost all cases semi-automatically. The work provides a tool for the community that can help to optimize AF ablation. In the future, the algorithm could be improved to be 100% automatic, although right now it is already useful and several clinical studies are underway using this tool.

title: Retracted: A Novel System for Prediction of Facemask and maintaining Social Distance in COVID
authors: E. Dinesh; S. Charanyameenachi; M. Shanmathi; A. S. Bhavisha
venue: 2022 International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Data Communication Systems (ICSCDS)
abstract: SARS stands for Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome, which is also known as COVID-19. Covid is an uncommonly overwhelming contamination that spreads through breathing dots from corrupted individuals talking, sneezing, or hacking. At whatever point you come into near contact with a polluted person or contact a contaminated surface or thing, the disease can spread rapidly. There's clearly no checking pro open to battle COVID-19, and the foremost sublime strategy for ensuring oneself against an sickness is to remain lost from it. Wearing a facemask that covers the nose and mouth in an open reach and washing hands routinely utilizing something like 70% alcohol based sanitizers are prescribed to diminish viral degradation. Significant Learning advancement has shown its capacity to see and arrange things by analyzing photographs. A collected picture data includes 20,000 photos that were consistently cropped in 224×224 pixels and had a 97 percent accuracy rate during the model's training. Utilizing Python and Open CV utilizing Tensor Stream, the developed system sees individuals wearing or not wearing a facemask and chooses the genuine separate between them. The detected informational stored in cloud. It raises an alert when it recognizes persons who aren't wearing a mask and snaps images of their faces. It is unconcerned with physical distance. This study will aid in preventing the virus from spreading and in preventing people from contracting it.

title: Real-time processing of electromyography signals using artificial neural networks
authors: S. Yair Suaid; M. Inés Pisarello; C. Torres Salinas; J. Emilio Monzón
venue: 2022 IEEE Biennial Congress of Argentina (ARGENCON)
abstract: The processing of electromyography (EMG) signals is complex due to the stochastic nature of the signal itself. Artificial neural networks (ANN) computationally implement a type of processing similar to that of the human brain, which is appropriate for these signals, and are one of the valid techniques used for their processing. Using supervised learning algorithms; with ANNs it is possible to identify patterns in EMG signal recordings. With this, it is possible to build an interface that allows us to interact with technological devices. In this work, a trained ANN is implemented using the records of 3 types of movement. The network must be able to identify: twisting of the wrist, extension of the fingers of the hand and contraction of the arm. Data acquisition and network implementation are performed using a microcontroller for signal conversion and a Python computational environment. A sequential network structure was established, whose output indicates the probability that the input corresponds to one of the patterns to be classified. A database was created for the training and validation of the network. Analyzing the results obtained by it, we see that a precision level of 88% was reached on the training set and 84% on the validation set, which shows the viability of this type of processing for pattern classification.

title: Systematic Evaluation of Hyperscale Cloud Providers Trustworthiness for Hosting Telco Workloads
authors: R. Pakrooh; C. Fung; L. Suárez; A. Jabbari
venue: 2026 IFIP Networking Conference (IFIP Networking)
abstract: Telecommunications companies (telcos) are currently transitioning critical workloads from private infrastructure to Hyperscale Cloud Providers (HCPs). Leveraging managed environments from providers such as Amazon, Google, and Microsoft enables substantial reductions in both CapEx and OpEx. However, making this decision is challenging as telcos find it difficult to trust these providers in hosting and protecting their valuable assets. Despite the extensive research on cloud providers trustworthiness, there are still some major challenges that need to be addressed.In this paper, we propose a novel framework to help telcos analyze the trustworthiness of different providers systematically and make informed decisions. This framework relies on public information to assess the trustworthiness of providers before making contracts considering the trustworthiness of information sources. We use Dirichlet distribution to model our belief regarding the value of each metric in the absence of fully trusted sources. This framework can be easily extended to include evidence from direct measurement, after making contracts, to update the metric values. Furthermore, we propose an adapted algorithm to update sources trustworthiness over time based on their provided pieces of evidence. Metrics expected values along with their confidence scores are combined using weighted geometric mean in each dimension and across dimensions to get the total trust score for each HCP.We implement a testbed using Python on top of a virtual network created in the OpenStack cloud computing infrastructure. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in comparing major HCPs. The resulting trust scores are influenced by both the set of evidence sources involved and the rate at which source trustworthiness evolves over time. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first granular framework for assessing the trustworthiness of HCPs based on public information.

title: Locational Marginal Price Forecasting Based on Deep Neural Networks and Prophet Techniques
authors: A. T. Mohamed; H. H. Aly; T. A. Little
venue: 2021 IEEE Electrical Power and Energy Conference (EPEC)
abstract: In many of the electricity markets in North America, the electricity prices are in terms of the locational marginal price (LMP) which reflects the cost of supplying the next MWh of electricity at a bus, considering transmission constraints. Electricity price forecasting provides vital information on system conditions to the independent system operator (ISO). It indicates important signals pertaining to the need of investing in the new generation, upgrading transmission, or reducing electricity consumption. Power suppliers and consumers use the forecasted price to optimize the profit in the day-ahead market and bilateral contracts. Facility owners rely on the forecasted price to make investment decisions. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) networks are applied to improve short-term (time series) LMP forecasting accuracy. Dataset from the ISO-NE power market is utilized in modeling and analysis in which the proposed techniques are applied using Matlab and Python software. Various methods are evaluated and compared, and the conclusions achieved show that LSTM has lower error rates and higher accuracy than the Prophet forecasting model in 24 h-ahead LMP forecasting.

title: ECG Data Compression Analysis by Employing Different Transforms in Orthogonal Transformation Technique
authors: D. Kaushal; V. Singh; P. Jain
venue: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: Using the orthogonal transformation method, this paper presents the performance analysis of FFT, DHT, DCT, and DST for ECG data compression. When the heart muscle contracts or expands as a response to the command signals coming from electrical stimulus in its electro-conduction system, an ECG signal is generated. In today's fast-paced life, ECG data compression is essential as today's lifestyle leads to many health problems. More storage space is required for research purposes or data transmission, and data compression utilizes memory storage effectively. The performance of each transform has been recorded by calculating compression ratio (CR) to measure the compression acquired, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to measure signal strength to the background noise, and percent rms difference (PRD) for error measurement. The parameters have been measured using Python and has been compared with the literature. The Discrete Cosine transform performed well compared to the rest in the orthogonal transformation method with a PRD of 4.80 at CR of 5.14 and an SNR of 26.36.

title: Blockchain Based Farmer’s Portal for Agri-Governance
authors: S. Khaja Shareef; M. Yashwanth; D. S. Vishnu; M. V. K. Varma; B. C. Vardhini
venue: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: Blockchain is a technology stores transaction confirmation in the form of crypto-currency. It develops the records of any digital asset transparent and unchangeable and works without involving any middlemen or third-party intermediary. They contribute security and set boundaries to the assets. This demonstrates how the farmer's portal uses blockchain technology to store footage of crop sales and purchases and to develop a model to maintain all the transactions between government initiatives and farmers based on farm subsidies. This farmer's portal designed on basis of blockchain helps those farmers to sell their products directly to the government and in receiving the subsidies without inclusion of any middle men or third-party sites. This helps the farmers in increasing the desired amount directly to themselves. It includes the farmers and government itself. The proposed solution designs an interface by using the python's integration with the blockchain system as a programming language will maintain the contract of trade to the advantage of vendors, farmers, and individuals. The information pertaining to farmers, the government, buying and selling an item, farm subsidies, and the total value of transactions is stored using this interface. Blockchain technology's immutability will make it easier for farmers to obtain the actual price of their harvested crops and reduce the cost of buying and selling crops, helps in receiving the subsidies compared to traditional methods and third-party involvement.

title: Optimizing System Loss through Data-Driven Inspection Deployment: A Cluster-Level Electricity Theft Analysis Approach
authors: J. M. Bunagan; R. C. Santos; K. Borja; A. S. Rosa; J. E. Lafuente; V. E. Marquez
venue: 2025 25th Conference of the Electric Power Supply Industry (CEPSI)
abstract: System loss is a persistent challenge in the power distribution industry, significantly affecting revenue assurance, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance. A major contributor to system loss is non-technical losses, which stem from unauthorized electricity consumption, including meter tampering and other kind of electricity thefts. This project harnesses large-scale data analytics to enhance inspection planning by analyzing customer and inspection datasets—each containing at least two million records. Through python-based data processing, we systematically assess past inspection results and identify customer clusters with the highest electricity theft hit rates. This targeted approach ensures that future inspection efforts maximize impact while minimizing resource deployment.The analytical workflow begins with data integration and preprocessing, ensuring consistency and accuracy across datasets. Advanced statistical methods and machine learning models are applied to uncover patterns in historical inspections and predict high-risk areas for future electricity thefts. Geographic clustering enables efficient segmentation of customers based on inspection outcomes, allowing for precise targeting of areas where unauthorized activities are most prevalent.A key deliverable of this project is an interactive heatmap, provided to area offices, which visually represents inspection results. This tool includes tooltips displaying critical metrics such as electricity theft hit rates, the number of thefts apprehended, and the total inspections conducted per cluster. By leveraging this geospatial intelligence, decision-makers can deploy field teams more strategically, prioritizing locations with the highest expected return on effort.The implementation of this data-driven strategy significantly improves the efficiency of inspection teams while optimizing resource allocation. By focusing on clusters with historically high electricity theft occurrences, the company reduces operational costs and enhances system loss mitigation. This approach also minimizes unnecessary inspections in low-risk areas, streamlining workforce utilization and improving overall operational efficiency. Additionally, this initiative aligns with key performance indicators (KPIs), particularly system loss reduction, which is critical for financial sustainability and regulatory adherence.The findings from this project contribute to a broader predictive analytics framework for power distribution management. Future enhancements could incorporate additional variables such as real-time consumption patterns, socio-economic factors, and smart meter data to further refine predictive accuracy. By continuously evolving analytical methodologies, the company can sustain and improve its proactive strategy in mitigating system loss.Ultimately, this project underscores the power of data-driven decision-making in utility management. By leveraging historical inspection and customer data, we establish an optimized framework for the strategic deployment of inspection resources. This initiative not only enhances the efficiency of detecting Violation of Contract (VOC) cases—a key indicator of potential unauthorized electricity use—but also significantly contributes to reducing system loss. As the power distribution sector advances toward digital transformation, projects like this set a foundation for a more intelligent, cost-effective, and sustainable approach to metering operations and revenue assurance.

title: Diagnosing Candidate Quality Bottlenecks in RL-Guided LLM Code Repair
authors: J. Zhang; G. Noh
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Recent Large Language Models (LLMs) have driven an intuitive expectation that automated program repair (APR) can be treated as a direct code-rewriting task. However, practical APR systems require generated candidates to be machine-usable, safely validated, and appropriately ranked. This paper uses an RL-guided repair loop as an instrumented diagnostic environment to separate correct-candidate availability from candidate selection. We evaluate all 40 Python programs in QuixBugs using four code-LLM families, four versioned output-contract conditions, and five fixed random seeds. The resulting 3,200 candidate-generation conditions were evaluated with public tests for plausible correctness and a separately defined 1,200-case augmented oracle for semantic correctness. All 40 programs and all prespecified runs were retained. Correct candidates were available in 173 of 3,200 conditions and for 30 of 40 programs, showing that availability was a necessary upstream constraint under the evaluated conditions. Static greedy selection improved the program-level correct-outcome rate over first selection by 10.0 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 23.3]; Holm-adjusted  $p=.25$ ), while the separate sequential comparison improved by 5.0 points (95% CI [0.0, 12.5]; Holm-adjusted  $p=.50$ ); neither effect was statistically established. These conclusions are limited to single-file Python algorithmic repair on QuixBugs and do not establish general superiority of RL, a selector, or an output representation.

title: From Shell to Service: Unified OAUTH/OIDC Enforcement in Microfrontend-Driven Systems
authors: K. Savajiyani
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: As enterprises decompose monolithic platforms into microfrontend (MFE) shells and independently deployed microservices, authentication and authorization boundaries fragment across dozens of runtime units. Existing literature addresses frontend composition and backend security as separate concerns; no unified architectural model governs identity enforcement, bot mitigation, and audit traceability across both layers simultaneously. This paper introduces the Unified Security Governance Framework (USGF), a cross-layer reference architecture that enforces consistent security contracts from the MFE shell through an API gateway to downstream microservices, serverless functions, and asynchronous event streams. USGF integrates Okta OIDC/OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for token-based identity propagation, reCAPTCHA v3 for bot-risk scoring at the frontend boundary, Kong JWT-validation plugins for gateway-layer claims enforcement, and OpenTelemetry distributed tracing with a canonical audit-event schema for end-to-end observability. The framework is evaluated within an enterprise-scale research environment configured to mirror real-world deployment patterns across Spring Boot microservices, Python FaaS functions, and Kafka event streams. Results demonstrate an 89% reduction in authentication-failure events, a 33-percentage-point improvement in bot-request interception rate, and complete audit coverage across crossapplication flows, at a P99 latency overhead of 33 ms over an unsecured baseline.

title: COVID Prevention Protocol with Attendance Management System
authors: S. Dinesh; G. Vignesh; E. Kaliappan
venue: 2022 Third International Conference on Intelligent Computing Instrumentation and Control Technologies (ICICICT)
abstract: Coronaviruses, a large family of distinct viruses, have recently become exceedingly prevalent, communicable, and harmful to the entire human race. It transmits from person to person by exhaling infected breath, which deposits virus droplets on various surfaces, which are subsequently inhaled by another person, who contracts the infection. As a result, we must safeguard ourselves and those around us from this predicament. You can take safety measures such as keeping a social distance, washing your hands every two hours, using disinfectants, and most importantly, wearing a mask. In recent years, wearing masks in public places has become widespread all over the world. As an attendance system is a mandatory part in every school, college and workplace we can utilize it to follow some standard covid prevention protocol. The paper’s goal is to create a system with covid preventive protocol along with the attendance management system. The covid preventive protocol includes Detection of the mask, Temperature Monitoring, and sanitization. To identify whether the face mask is present or not, CNN a deep learning algorithm is used with the help of python code. My CNN model achieves better accuracy than Alexnet and LeNet which are the predefined framework of convolutional neural network.

title: Study on Minimum Annual Electricity Bill of a Campus Microgrid Using the Sparrow Search Algorithm and Bin Packing Method
authors: W. -T. Huang; W. -C. Lin; K. -C. Yao; L. -C. Li; C. -S. Huang
venue: 2023 9th International Conference on Control, Decision and Information Technologies (CoDIT)
abstract: This paper aims to solve the minimum annual electricity bill problem of a campus microgrid with distributed generation and a battery energy storage system via the proposed optimal hybrid approach with sparrow search algorithm (SSA) and bin packing method (BPM). First, the hourly, daily, monthly, and annual electricity bill computing modules were built. The historical electrical consumption and photovoltaic generation were analyzed to statistic the net load distribution and duration over one year. Next, the time-of-use rate for high-voltage customers with demand charge and energy charging of Taipower for the high-voltage campus microgrid was formulated as an optimization function and coded in python language. The charging and discharging schedule of the 1 MW/1.26 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS), according to the annual net load, were considered in this minimum annual electricity bill problem. We obtained the optimal contract capacity and the corresponding minimum annual electricity bill. The optimal hybrid approach was applied to solve this optimization problem. The results demonstrate that the proposed method could effectively solve the annual minimum electricity bill problem.

title: Sensor-Infused Emperor Penguin Optimized Deep Maxout Network for Paralyzed Person Monitoring
authors: J. Yang; R. Hu; C. Wu; G. Jiang; R. I. Alkanhel; H. Elmannai
venue: IEEE Sensors Journal
abstract: Paralyzed people must maintain proper posture to prevent respiratory problems, pressure sores, and muscular contractures. A paralyzed person may slip out of their wheelchair several times as a result of poor sitting position. To overcome these challenges, a novel Emperor Penguin optimized sensor-Infused wheelChair (EPIC) framework has been proposed to constantly monitor the real-time posture of the paralyzed person’s health state. The proposed model aims to monitor wheelchair posture and health in real time, which can automatically detect posture issues, providing timely alerts and feedback to the user via a mobile application. The proposed framework utilizes the emperor penguin optimizer (EPO) algorithm for feature selection to improve the accuracy of posture detection. A deep maxout network (DMN) analyzes the features to predict the posture of the wheelchair user patient. The proposed EPIC framework has been assessed using a Python simulator. The effectiveness of the proposed EPIC framework has been determined using evaluation metrics, such as precision, specificity, accuracy, and sensitivity. The proposed EPIC technique advances the overall accuracy by 10.1%, 7.73%, and 2.84% better than posture recognition, graphic user interface (GUI), and independent component analysis-kantorovich distance (ICA-KD), respectively.

title: ICS/SCADA Device Recognition: A Hybrid Communication-Patterns and Passive-Fingerprinting Approach
authors: A. T. Al Ghazo; R. Kumar
venue: 2019 IFIP/IEEE Symposium on Integrated Network and Service Management (IM)
abstract: The Industrial Control System (ICS) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems are the backbones for monitoring and supervising factories, power grids, water distribution systems, nuclear plants, and other critical infrastructures. These systems are installed by third party contractors, maintained by site engineers, and operate for a long time. This makes tracing the documentation of the systems' changes and updates challenging since some of their components' information (type, manufacturer, model, etc.) may not be up-to-date, leading to possibly unaccounted security vulnerabilities in the systems. Device recognition is useful first step in vulnerability identification and defense augmentation, but due to the lack of full traceability in case of legacy ICS/SCADA systems, the typical device recognition based on document inspection is not applicable. In this paper, we propose a hybrid approach involving the mix of communication-patterns and passive-fingerprinting to identify the unknown devices' types, manufacturers, and models. The algorithm uses the ICS/SCADA devices's communication-patterns to recognize the control hierarchy levels of the devices. In conjunction, certain distinguishable features in the communication-packets are used to recognize the device manufacturer, and model. We have implemented this hybrid approach in Python, and tested on traffic data from a water treatment SCADA testbed in Singapore (iTrust).

title: Interpretable Supervised Machine Learning Models For Fetal Abnormalities Prediction
authors: E. E. Y. Wilson; M. F. Kalyango; J. Nakatumba-Nabende
venue: 2023 First International Conference on the Advancements of Artificial Intelligence in African Context (AAIAC)
abstract: Prenatal treatment is complicated by fetal anomalies, thus timely intervention and better results depend on accurate prognosis. With the use of ultrasound, echocardiography, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), pregnant women and the developing fetus are medically monitored at certain stages. In this research, machine learning’s ability to understand and build methods that leverage data to improve computer performance on tasks is implemented on medical data of fetuses recorded during antenatal visits to identify certain features or factors that may lead to fetal abnormalities either during pregnancy or childbirth by using supervised learning techniques. The health data recordings were read using Cardiotocograms (CTGs), a simple and cost-accessible equipment. Ultrasound pulses were used, and the CTG was used to measure the reaction in order to determine the uterine contractions, fetal movements, FHR(fetal heart rate), and additional factors.Since AI models have demonstrated a high degree of precision in terms of their suitability for the health sector, comprehending the information these models rely on in order to make such correct decisions has become just as crucial as the models’ accuracy.This paper develops predictive models after analysing output of a Python library framework which is a machine learning(ML) approach that implements various algorithms with less user input in predicting fetal abnormalities. SHAP and LIME explainable AI (XAI) techniques were used for model accountability. Five trained classification models were developed and results assessed. LGBM classifier achieved a high accuracy of 96.71%, and GaussianNB of low accuracy 82.16% .

title: A Comparitive Evaluation Of Custom CNN, Sequential CNN & Dense-Net Models to forecast Dementia
authors: M. Sobhana; K. Hindu; N. Girishma; P. S. Bhavani; S. Rajeswari
venue: 2023 Second International Conference on Augmented Intelligence and Sustainable Systems (ICAISS)
abstract: Dementia is a very common neurological condition that affects the elderly. Mild cognitive impairment sufferers run the risk of contracting this illness. It steadily worsens from mild to severe, making it challenging for the person to complete any task without assistance. To accurately assess the patient’s state and begin receiving intense medical care, a dementia diagnosis must be made as soon as possible. Manual diagnosis takes a lot of work, takes a long time, and is prone to error. In this study, three CNN models Dense-net, Sequential, and Custom Convolutional Neural Network are evaluated for the diagnosis of dementia. All these models’ performances were compared, and results were found. Sequential model obtained an accuracy of 83%, Dense-Net achieved an accuracy of 88% and the Customized Sequential model achieved an accuracy of 98%. Using Python Flask, a web application that offers the best graphical user interface is further developed. The graphical user interface can upload the MRI scan images and provide these images to the best trained model which predicts whether the person is suffering from dementia or not and can categorize the stage of the disease.

title: Harnessing AI and Machine Learning to Transform English Language Learning Experiences
authors: S. B; P.Bindhu; M. Mythili; P. V. Kumar; E. Pearlin; N. K. Hamid
venue: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This study presents a methodology for evaluating argumentative essays from English language learners (ELLs) in grades 8 through 12, utilizing the ELLIPSE corpus. The essays are assessed across six critical metrics: coherence, syntax, vocabulary, phraseology, grammar, and conventions, with ratings from 1.0 to 5.0. The process begins with data collection, followed by preprocessing steps to prepare the text for machine learning. This includes removing punctuation, stopwords, stemming, lemmatization, and expanding contractions to enhance text quality for analysis. Advanced feature extraction techniques are then applied, utilizing word embeddings to convert textual data into dense vector representations. These embeddings capture the syntactic and semantic nuances of the text, making it suitable for machine learning models. The vectorized data is input into Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, which are adept at handling sequential data. LSTMs manage information flow through cell states and gates, allowing them to capture long-term dependencies in the text effectively. The LSTM network processes the text sequentially, leveraging previous words to make informed classification decisions. The resulting model provides high-accuracy classifications of essays based on the six metrics, offering insights into learners' proficiency levels. This methodology demonstrates a robust application of AI and machine learning in enhancing English language learning, with potential uses in personalized education and automated assessment systems. The study highlights the effectiveness of integrating advanced feature extraction and sequential modeling techniques to assess and improve language proficiency among students. The proposed Word Embedding-based LSTM Model, however, gave out a great result where it produced an accuracy of 98% and it is implemented in python.

title: Early Prediction Model for Anemia in Infants Using Clinical Data from Perú Applying Supervised Machine Learning Algorithms
authors: J. Rivera; D. Cardenas; J. L. Castillo-Sequera; L. Wong
venue: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Anemia is a disease that is always present from early stages; children are the most prone to contracting it from birth if it's not diagnosed, which can lead to more severe illnesses. Therefore, a predictive model is proposed for the detection of anemia in infants using their clinical data. The Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM) methodology is employed, along with Analysis Services for the Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) process and four Machine Learning (ML) algorithms: Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF). All four phases of CRISP-DM were utilized: Business Understanding, Data Understanding, Data Preparation, Modeling, and Evaluation. The dataset used consists of 400,000 records related to the medical history of children from a healthcare institution in Peru, from which 27 variables were selected. The results showed that the DT algorithm performed better, achieving an AUC-ROC Curve greater than 93%, and the “Scikit Learn” library for ML in Python facilitated obtaining the results.

title: CommonRoad-Reach: A Toolbox for Reachability Analysis of Automated Vehicles
authors: E. I. Liu; G. Würsching; M. Klischat; M. Althoff
venue: 2022 IEEE 25th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC)
abstract: In recent years, reachability analysis has gained considerable popularity in motion planning and safeguarding of automated vehicles (AVs). While existing tools for reachability analysis mainly focus on general-purpose algorithms for formal verification of dynamical systems, a toolbox tailored to AV-specific applications is not yet available. In this study, we present CommonRoad-Reach, which is a toolbox that integrates different methods for computing reachable sets and extracting driving corridors for AVs in dynamic traffic scenarios. Our toolbox provides a Python interface and an efficient C++implementation for real-time applications. The toolbox is integrated within the CommonRoad benchmark suite and is available at commonroad.in.tum.de.

title: Automatic Processor Customization for Zero-Overhead Online Software Verification
authors: H. Lu; A. Forin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
abstract: The PSL-to-Verilog (P2V) compiler can translate a set of assertions about a block-structured software program into a hardware design to be executed concurrently with the program. The assertions validate the correctness of the software program without altering the program's temporal behavior in any way, a result never previously achieved by any online model-checking system. Additionally, the techniques and implementations described apply to any general purpose program and the absence of execution overhead renders the system ideal for the verification and debugging of real-time systems. Assertions are expressed in a simple subset of the property specification language (PSL), an IEEE standard originally intended for the behavioral specification of hardware designs. The target execution system is the eMIPS processor, a dynamically self-extensible processor realized with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). The system can concurrently execute and check multiple programs at a time. Assertions are compiled into eMIPS Extensions, which are loaded by the operating system software into a portion of the FPGA, and discarded once the program terminates. If an assertion is violated, the program receives an exception, otherwise, it executes fully unaware of its verifier. The software program is not modified in any way. It can be compiled separately with full optimizations and executes with or without the corresponding hardware checker. The P2V compiler, implemented in Python, generates code for the implementation of the eMIPS processor running on the Xilinx ML401 development board. It is currently used to verify software properties in areas such as testing, debugging, intrusion detection, and the behavioral verification of concurrent and real-time programs.

title: Data Analytics and Machine Learning Methods, Techniques and Tool for Model-Driven Engineering of Smart IoT Services
authors: A. Moin
venue: 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering: Companion Proceedings (ICSE-Companion)
abstract: This doctoral dissertation proposes a novel approach to enhance the development of smart services for the Internet of Things (IoT) and smart Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). The proposed approach offers abstraction and automation to the software engineering processes, as well as the Data Analytics (DA) and Machine Learning (ML) practices. This is realized in an integrated and seamless manner. We implement and validate the proposed approach by extending an open source modeling tool, called ThingML. ThingML is a domain-specific language and modeling tool with code generation for the IoT/CPS domain. Neither ThingML nor any other IoT/CPS modeling tool supports DA/ML at the modeling level. Therefore, as the primary contribution of the doctoral dissertation, we add the necessary syntax and semantics concerning DA/ML methods and techniques to the modeling language of ThingML. Moreover, we support the APIs of several ML libraries and frameworks for the automated generation of the source code of the target software in Python and Java. Our approach enables platform-independent, as well as platform-specific models. Further, we assist in carrying out semiautomated DA/ML tasks by offering Automated ML (AutoML), in the background (in expert mode), and through model-checking constraints and hints at design-time. Finally, we consider three use case scenarios from the domains of network security, smart energy systems and energy exchange markets.

title: Approximation Methods for Simulation and Equivalence Checking of Noisy Quantum Circuits
authors: M. Huang; J. Guan; W. Fang; M. Ying
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
abstract: In the current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era, simulating and verifying noisy quantum circuits is crucial but faces challenges such as quantum state explosion and complex noise representations, constraining simulation and equivalence checking to circuits with a limited number of qubits. This article introduces an approximation algorithm for simulating and assessing the equivalence of noisy quantum circuits, specifically designed to improve scalability under low-noise conditions. The approach utilizes a novel tensor network (TN) diagram combined with singular value decomposition to approximate the tensors of quantum noises. The implementation is based on Google’s TensorNetwork Python package for contraction. Experimental results on realistic quantum circuits with realistic hardware noise models indicate that our algorithm can simulate and check the equivalence of quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) circuits with around 200 qubits and 20 noise operators, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches in scalability and speed.

title: Emotion-Aware Music Recommendation using CNN, BERT, and DQN for Real-Time Personalization
authors: A. D; J. S. W; M. Rifaz S; S. M; N. V
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications (ICSCSA)
abstract: The focus of this project is to work on a recommendation engine that learns and responds to the emotional needs of the listener. The conventional music recommender has been enduring for a very long time now, with the integration of AI in recent days. These algorithms learn the user preferences over time and analyze their listening patterns to follow up on the recommendation the next time they start with a listening session. To address this problem of suggesting songs based on emotions we concentrate on the emotion analysis of the listener. There are several ways and methods that can be used to detect the emotion of the listener, but the one easily available factor that can be read and analyzed is the facial expressions. Algorithms like Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) can be used to extract the different features of facial emotions expressed by the contraction and relaxation of different facial muscles. Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) to categorize the songs into different emotions that aligns with the previously read facial emotions [happy, sad, neutral, angry, disgust]. The Pygame library of Python can then be used to combine the results obtained from the algorithms mentioned above to play the song that aligns with the emotion of the listener. To ensure that the algorithm functions well, and the user is satisfied with the recommendations, Deep Q Networks can be implemented so that the user preference are analyzed and when found that the song that is being played does not satisfy the users’ needs or is disliked by the user, the system will understand the uncertain decision made by the system must be avoided in the future. Since the system not only understands the emotions of the listener but also if the listener is satisfied with the recommendations of the system, it can alter its recommendation preferences over time, making it more personalized and appealing to the user.

title: Multi-task Convolution Neural Network towards Detection and Classification of Cardiovascular Disease on Leveraging Color Fundus Retina Images
authors: N. S; V. K
venue: 2025 First International Conference of Advances in Engineering and Computing Technologies for Sustainable Development (AECTSD)
abstract: cardiovascular disease is one of the most prevalent diseases which causing high mortality rate among various age groups across the world. According to world health organization, addressing cardiovascular diseases in the early stages can highly prevent and reduce the mortality rate. Thus, it becomes mandatory to perform early diagnosis of the cardiovascular disease with respect to heart condition. Various manual and automated researches have been performed to early diagnosis of heart condition through multiple medical examination in form blood test, ECG, X-Ray, CT scan, MRI Scan and Angiography. However, those approaches involve invasive procedure and it is considered as expensive and complexity for early diagnosis. Hence it becomes mandatory to design a simple cost effective non -invasive tool to be employed to diagnosis of the heart condition with high scalability. In this paper, a new early cardiovascular disease diagnosis approach is performed on integration of the artificial intelligences process the color fundus image of eye which acquired through color fundus photograph. A Novel artificial intelligence technique entitled as Multi-Task Convolution Neural Network is designed and implemented to the process the acquired color fundus image of eye is to detect and classify the heart disease. Initially acquired color fundus retinal image is preprocessed using wiener filter to remove the noise and Contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization for image enhancement. Preprocessed image has been projected to dual branch convolution neural network. Dual branch convolution neural network contains U-Net for artery –vein segmentation and ResNet architecture towards extraction of the feature in the AV segments and to classify that feature into different cardiovascular disease classes. U-Net architecture composed of the encoder (contraction path) and decoder (expansion path) sections. Encoder section of U-Net is augmented with ResNet backbone to eliminate the vanishing gradient challenges in deeper layer and to preserve the fine-grained details of the feature. ResNet backbone contains different block with residual connection to capture the hierarchical contextual feature related to blood vessel (Artery vein characteristics) at different resolutions in different regions of the fundus image through process of the down-sampling in the convolution layers and max pooling layer on generating the feature map while decoder section reconstructs the segmentation map through upsampling process (Transposed convolution or bilinear interpolation) in upsampling layers on combining features of the encoder through skip connection. Segmentation map (artery vein map) is projected to the fully connected layer of the Residual Network for classification of the segmented map. Finally, fully connected layer composed of softmax function is used to identify the retinal biomarker to associate the different cardiovascular diseases. Experimental and performance analysis of the proposed model is performed using benchmark Fundus AvSeg15 dataset in the python environment. On experimental analysis, it is proved that proposed model produces 98.2% accuracy in detecting the cardiovascular diseases.

title: Advancements in Chatbot Technology for Enhanced Customer Support in Online Retail
authors: N. Keerthi Kumar; K. Maheswari; A. Abinaya; J. Ramya; P. K. Ande; C. P. Ramaian
venue: 2024 Ninth International Conference on Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics (ICONSTEM)
abstract: In order to improve customer service and boost sales, this paper describes the creation of an ecommerce sales chatbot. In order to grasp natural language, the system employs machine learning. It is based on a chatbot that is modular. Framework. There are several parts to the system. A web-based framework for natural language teaching comes first. Chat bots are employed in a variety of industries, including e-commerce, healthcare, and education. The objective of this venture is to make Hebron, an online chatbot for the Contract College People group Shopping center. Python and Respond are both utilized in the chatbot's creation. Conventional customer service chatbots frequently copy human discussion, yet they have serious protection and data adaptability issues. Here, we present SuperAgent, a customer support chatbot that utilizes broad and promptly open internet business data.

title: Equilibrium Index and Core Node Set of New Social Networks
authors: L. Han; Y. Cui; C. Dou; N. Du; S. Han; J. You
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: In the last fifteen years, the network-based new media has greatly promoted the development of social networks, therefore it becomes the main form of social composition. Research on social networks commenced a long time ago and revealed meaningful features of the old social network. However, in the new social networks, group members are almost 24-h online and can exchange various information that cannot be dynamically handled or described by the most of the existing studies. In this paper, we construct a formula to calculate the amount of the data dissemination of a node. Thereafter, we present participation equilibrium index formula and maximum equilibrium index formula that can measure the dynamic equilibrium of social networks even for different topics. With these formulas, we define λ-set and core node set of a social group and also present algorithms to work out the two sets. To evaluate our theory and method, we have developed SN-Python-I that can filter and calculate the amount of data exchanged by any node in any group. Based on a contract signed in 2013 with Ali and Tencent, we are permitted to track 300 actual groups for the past three years. Real data of those group reveals that equilibrium index as well as λ-set and core node set of social network change with the time, ages, topics, and classification of the groups. What's more, monthly equilibrium index can also indicate life stages of a group. Those significant properties and rules have not yet been revealed by traditional social network models.

title: Preconditions and Postconditions as Design Constraints for LLM Code Generation
authors: L. Newcomb; A. Newcomb; O. Ochoa
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced automated code generation, but current methods predominantly rely on natural language descriptions during prompting. This approach encounters challenges when handling complex, class-level software generation tasks due to inherent ambiguity and under-specification. On the other hand, few studies have investigated how formal software engineering constraints, such as explicit preconditions and postconditions as part of the Design-by-Contract paradigm, influence class-level generation tasks. This work addresses this gap through a structured evaluation of six state-of-the-art LLMs generating complete software implementations of a medium complexity system from systematically designed class-level specifications. Results demonstrate that incorporating explicit design constraints during prompting significantly boosts initial generation accuracy (measured via the pass@k metric), particularly in Python but also in C++. Models with fewer parameters saw especially pronounced benefits. These findings suggest integrating structured software engineering constraints and design principles into LLM-based code generation workflows to enhance accuracy and maintainability in automated software projects.

title: Intelli-Query: A Large Language Model System for Semantic Retrieval and Document Understanding
authors: S. Bansal; T. Choudhary; R. S. Pal
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Innovative Practices in Technology and Management (ICIPTM)
abstract: The rapid growth of unstructured digital documents has created significant challenges in retrieving accurate information using traditional keyword-based search systems. Organizations often struggle to efficiently interpret lengthy reports, contracts, and policy documents, resulting in increased manual effort and delayed decision-making. This paper presents INTELLI-QUERY, an intelligent document understanding and semantic retrieval platform designed to provide context-aware query responses. The system integrates a Python-based backend, transformer-based sentence embeddings, FAISS vector indexing, and a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). Intelli-Query automatically ingests documents, performs preprocessing and semantic chunking, and stores embeddings in a vector database to enable similarity-based retrieval. When a user submits a natural-language query, the system identifies intent, retrieves the most relevant document sections, and generates evidence-grounded responses. The platform also supports multi-question batch processing and structured JSON outputs for downstream applications. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that embedding-based retrieval combined with LLM reasoning significantly improves contextual relevance and reduces hallucination compared to direct LLM answering. The system achieved a context relevance score of 0.81 and reduced incorrect responses by approximately 70 %. This work highlights the effectiveness of combining semantic search and language models in transforming static documents into interactive knowledge systems, enabling efficient enterprise information access and supporting accurate decision-making.

title: An Intelligent Attention-Driven Convolutional Neural Network for Legal Compliance Analysis of ToS Statements
authors: S. Kokila; D. K. Hanirex
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Knowledge Discovery in Concurrent Engineering (ICECONF)
abstract: The problem with Terms of Service (ToS) is that it is a difficult task to enforce them are often vague and hard to comprehend, not allowing the end-users to determine the most important requirements and risks. To address this issue, a novel attention-based convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture is proposed to analyze and automate ToS statements compliance. The model also includes contextual attention to signal clauses of legal interest, and convolutional layers identify the semantic structure. A curated dataset of ToS agreements was used in a variety of service domains, and trained and validated their system through real-time simulation in a Python-based TensorFlow setup. The proposed algorithm has 94.2% accuracy, 93.5% precision, 92.8% recall, with an F1-score of 93.1, which is far better than existing baselines. Its greater efficiency was evidenced by an evaluation of its efficiency against methods recently used, whether this model can be applied to compliance monitoring systems, whereby one can transparently, interpretably, and automatically assess compliance obligations of the contract.

title: NEITH: Networked Evidence Integrity for Telemetry Hashing
authors: M. El-Hadedy
venue: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Secure IoT, Assured and Trusted Computing (SATC)
abstract: Autonomous platforms rely on high-rate multisensor telemetry (e.g., Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and LiDAR) for safety, accountability, and post-incident reconstruction, yet disputes often reduce to a basic question: what data was actually retained. This paper presents NEITH, a lightweight window-commitment contract that makes retention externally checkable without trusted storage or full log replication. NEITH partitions time into windows of length $\Delta$. Within each window, each ingested chunk is mapped to a leaf position from ingestionobservable metadata (sensor identifier and per-window index) and aggregated with standard hash functions and extendableoutput functions (XOFs) in a Merkle-style tree, yielding one constant-size root $R_{t}$ (32 bytes) per window. Later, a verifier checks retention claims from the published roots and a short inclusion proof ($R_{t}, c, \pi$); an optional order rule also makes within-window reordering detectable. NEITH runs on a small edge Kubernetes cluster and is evaluated with u-blox GNSS and Youyeetoo LiDAR streams plus bursty synthetic producers. Over 32 consecutive windows $(\Delta=10 ~\mathrm{s})$, the system emits one root per window and stays aligned to the window schedule. Microbenchmarks on 8 KiB leaves show that widely used tree-hash designs sustain $\mathbf{5 - 2 6 ~ M B} / \mathbf{s}$ under 1/8/32 concurrent connections, whereas a reference Python ASCON-XOF baseline costs $\approx 760 ~\text{ms}$ per 8 KiB leaf, indicating when the no-stutter timing bound cannot be met on this software stack.
