However, these requirements are challenging to achieve due to complex I/O access path and resource management at the system level, lack of support from preemptive scheduling at I/O hardware level, and missing an effective energy management method. In this paper, we propose a new framework, I/O-GUARD, which reconstructs the system architecture of I/O virtualization, bringing a dedicated hardware hypervisor to handle resource management throughout the system. The hypervisor improves system real-time performance by enabling preemptive scheduling in I/O virtualization with both analytical and experimental real-time guarantees. Furthermore, we also present a dedicated energy management unit to adjust I/O-GUARD's dynamic energy using frequency scaling. Associated with that, a frequency identification algorithm is proposed to find the appropriate executing frequency at run-time. As shown in experiments, I/O-GUARD simultaneously improves the predictability, performance and energy-efficiency compared to the state-of-the-art I/O virtualization.

title: Real-Time Streaming Application for IoT Using Raspberry Pi and Handheld Devices
authors: J. Filteau; S. J. Lee; A. Jung
venue: 2018 IEEE Global Conference on Internet of Things (GCIoT)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) is in the spotlight because its applications positively impact everyday quality of life. This study aims to develop a cost-effective solution to real time video streaming by using a low-cost ARM (Advanced RISC Machines)-based computer, i.e. Raspberry Pi (RPi). We developed a simple streaming server written in Java that runs efficiently on the RPi and showed that the RPi can support streaming services to multiple devices at once. We also developed a light-weight android application that the server can stream to. The client and server communicate via JSON (JavaScript Object Notation). We divided high quality video into image files with the jpg format, into packets and then transmitted them to multiple handheld devices simultaneously. We conclude that our system anchored in a low-cost ARM-based computer can retain quality of service (QoS) regarding video streaming to multiple handheld devices.

title: Formal verification of Fischer’s real-time mutual exclusion protocol by the OTS/CafeOBJ method
authors: M. Nakamura; S. Higashi; K. Sakakibara; a. Ogata
venue: 2020 59th Annual Conference of the Society of Instrument and Control Engineers of Japan (SICE)
abstract: Fischer's protocol is a well-known real-time mutual exclusion protocol for multiple processes. The mutual exclusiveness is guaranteed by treating time aspects of transitions. In such a multitask real-time system, since processes run concurrently, the size of the state space grows exponentially. It is not easy to verify time constraints of a give system. Formal descriptions of multitask real-time systems may help us to verify time constraints formally with computer supports. In this paper, as a case study of the OTS/CafeOBJ method, we model Fischer's protocol as an observational transition system, describe it in CafeOBJ algebraic specification language, and verify that different processes do not enter the critical section at the same time by the proof score method based on equational reasoning implemented in CafeOBJ interpreter.

title: Implementing a Self-Timed Low-Power Java Accelerator for Network-on-Chip Applications
authors: Z. Liang; J. Plosila; L. Yan; K. Sere
venue: 2006 Seventh International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Computing, Applications and Technologies (PDCAT'06)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced self-timed Java accelerator core which has extremely low power consumption while providing sufficient performance for even the most demanding real-time telecommunication and multimedia applications. The goal is that the accelerator can be directly attached to any general-purpose processor core running some Java-intensive application software. Asynchronous self-timed circuit technology, where timing is based on local handshakes between circuit blocks instead of a global clock signal, provides a promising platform for obtaining a highly modular low-power Java accelerator implementation

title: Design and Implementation of Scalable AI-Driven Event Processing Systems Using Java, Apache Kafka, and Cloud-Native Architectures
authors: R. Namburi
venue: 2026 International Conference on Computing Theory and Wireless Communications (ICCTWC)
abstract: Real-time event-driven systems are increasingly critical in modern distributed applications, particularly in domains requiring high-throughput data processing and lowlatency decision-making. This paper presents the design and implementation of a scalable AI-driven event processing architecture leveraging Java-based micro services, Apache Kafka, and cloud-native platforms such as AWS. The proposed system integrates machine learning models into streaming pipelines to enable intelligent event classification, anomaly detection, and predictive analytics. The architecture employs Spring Boot micro services, Kafka-based messaging, and containerized deployment using Kubernetes for scalability and resilience. Performance evaluation demonstrates improved throughput, reduced latency, and enhanced fault tolerance. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining AI with event driven architectures for next-generation distributed systems.

title: Implementation of CNN on Zynq based FPGA for Real-time Object Detection
authors: A. Sharma; V. Singh; A. Rani
venue: 2019 10th International Conference on Computing, Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
abstract: The aim of this work is to implement a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) using a Python framework on Xilinx® Zynq® based Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). And the prototype is used to tackle the challenging problem of real-time object detection in computer vision. Pre-trained CNN models are implemented using Tensorflow Application Programming Interface (API). The models are then implemented on Xilinx® Zynq® based FPGA using Python productivity for Zynq (PYNQ). The versatility of this approach is tested on four state-of-the-art object detectors based on the classifiers i.e. mobilenet v1 and inception v2 and the meta-architectures i.e. SSD and Faster R-CNN which have been trained on MS-COCO dataset. System functionality is compared on the basis of system latency, detection accuracy and ease of implementation on ARM® embedded mobile platforms. It is observed from the results and real-time frame rate, SSD with inception v2 model is suitable for the intended application. This hardware software co-design approach forms the basis of FPGA based hardware accelerators.

title: Edge-Cloud Latency Optimization: A Priority-Based Scheduling Framework with Dynamic VM Allocation
authors: E. A. Mattar; P. Kumar Dutta; P. Bhattacharya; J. J. P. C. Rodrigues
venue: 2025 10th International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Technologies (SpliTech)
abstract: The proliferation of real-time data from Internet of Things (IoT) devices has posed significant challenges to traditional cloud-centric resource management. In particular, latency constraints and overload issues arise when large volumes of sensor data are continuously transmitted to remote cloud servers for processing. In this paper, we propose a novel framework that integrates priority-based data scheduling with dynamic virtual machine (VM) allocation in edge-cloud environments. Our approach employs an integrated flow queue at the edge node to eliminate inefficiencies associated with multi-queue systems. Three scheduling algorithms (static priority, dynamic priority, and integrated priority) are presented to classify and process data based on urgency and sensor type. The edge node handles high-priority tasks locally, while time-tolerant tasks are delegated to cloud VMs. Using real-world sensor data—including heartbeat and body temperature—we demonstrate that our proposed model significantly reduces latency and optimizes resource utilization compared to existing solutions. Our results suggest that this framework can be a scalable and robust solution for emerging IoT applications requiring real-time data processing.

title: Comprehensive Assessment of Small Batch Advanced Metering Infrastructure Utilization on Java Region to Support Indonesian Smart Grid Systems
authors: M. H. Prakoso; F. Irawan; A. M. Sufianto; D. Rediansyah
venue: 2023 4th International Conference on High Voltage Engineering and Power Systems (ICHVEPS)
abstract: Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) is the breakthrough path to implement the Indonesian smart grid system. The topology of small batch AMI utilization in the Java Region consists of a smart meter, communication media, data concentrator unit, head-end system, and meter data management system. By applying this technology, it can allow a government state-owned electricity company (PLN) to enable a two-way real-time energy monitoring system for supporting smart grid applications. It also has other benefits, such as simplifying the billing collection process and providing realtime event notification to monitor energy meter activities. On Java Regional Business, PLN has implemented AMI in three different locations (Bandung, Jakarta, and Surabaya). The goal of this small batch AMI implementation in Java Regional Business is to provide pre-commercial references and several evaluations for a future large-scale rollout implementation. The evaluation of small batch AMI implementation in Java regional businesses will be discussed, along with a deep dive into the preproduction process, customer installation, and performance evaluation. The end results of this evaluation will allow PLN to have a better view of a forthcoming large-scale project of advanced metering infrastructure to support smart grid system development in Indonesia.

title: Time Predictable CPU and DMA Shared Memory Access
authors: C. Pitter; M. Schoeberl
venue: 2007 International Conference on Field Programmable Logic and Applications
abstract: In this paper, we propose a first step towards a time predictable computer architecture for single-chip multiprocessing (CMP). CMP is the actual trend in server and desktop systems. CMP is even considered for embedded realtime systems, where worst-case execution time (WCET) estimates are of primary importance. We attack the problem of WCET analysis for several processing units accesing a shared resource (the main memory) by support from the hardware. In this paper, we combine a time predictable Java processor and a direct memory access (DMA) unit with a regular access pattern (VGA controller). We analyze and evaluate different arbitration schemes with respect to schedulability analysis and WCET analysis. We also implement the various combinations in an FPGA. An FPGA is the ideal platform to verify the different concepts and evaluate the results by running applications with industrial background in real hardware.

title: RTDroid: A Design for Real-Time Android
authors: Y. Yan; S. Cosgrove; V. Anand; A. Kulkarni; S. H. Konduri; S. Y. Ko; L. Ziarek
venue: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
abstract: This paper presents our work on the inception of RTDroid, a variant of Android that provides predictability to Android applications. Although there has been much interest in adopting Android in real-time contexts, surprisingly little work has been done to examine the suitability of the Android franework layer for real-time systems. Existing work only provides solutions to traditional problems, including adding support for real-time garbage collection at the virtual machine layer as well as kernel-level real-time scheduling and resource management. While it is critical to address these issues, it is by no means sufficient. After all, Android is a vast system that is more than a Java virtual machine and a kernel. Thus, this paper goes beyond existing work and examines the internals of Android, the Android programming model, libraries, and core systems services. We discuss the implications and challenges of adapting Android constructs and core system services for real-time and present a solution for each. Our system is unique in that it redesigns Androids internal components, replaces Androids Dalvik VM with a real-time VM, and leverages off-the-shelf real-time OSes. We demonstrate the feasibility and predictability of our solution on three different platforms. The evaluation results show that our design can successfully provide predictability to Android applications even under heavy loads.

title: Real Time Ethernet Control Communication for Robotic Arm Application by Using Raspberry-Pi
authors: A. Waingankar; P. C. Bhaskar
venue: 2018 Fourth International Conference on Computing Communication Control and Automation (ICCUBEA)
abstract: In this paper, real time control communication using Ethernet control communication is proposed. The aim is to develop this on network level. And also to include Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) implementation on the Ethernet platform for robotic arm application. The transferring data also includes various platforms as the medium of communication between FPGA board and the robotic arm. Many researcher's used Arduino as a controller and the results of time delay for Ethernet communication was considered to decide the better platform for communication. In this paper the Raspberry-Pi considered for the result of the average data packet delay between Raspberry-Pi and FPGA board is lower in comparison to Arduino board.

title: IO Virtualization for Real Time Automotive Systems
authors: G. Sriramakrishnan; M. Mody; G. Shurtz; C. Fuoco; K. Chitnis; N. Devshatwar; D. Steiss; J. Bergsagel; J. Jones; P. S. Y A
venue: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Virtualization is common in enterprise systems to isolate multiple server applications using the same underlying HW. In automotive systems virtualization is fast becoming table stakes to isolate safety applications like ADAS (Advanced Driver Assist System) and infotainment using the same underlying SOC. This presents unique challenges related to peripheral IO virtualization, not seen in enterprise systems, like deterministic latency to external memory (<5 cycles) and high data throughput (6-10GB/s for real-time camera's and display's. Traditional approach to peripheral virtualization involves usage of a centralized IOMMU using 2-level page table with a table walk through, which make the scheme non-deterministic and lower throughput. This paper proposes a automotive friendly approach to peripheral IO virtualization, using multiple innovations like, HW engine for level 1 deterministic scatter-gather operation via Peripheral Address Translation (PAT) unit, level 2 virtual machine context aware translation via Peripheral Virtualization Unit (PVU), and ability for these schemes to co-exists with tradition IOMMU schemes for non-real time traffic. The proposed virtualization system is implemented on the Jacinto 7 platform to virtualize a multi-camera ADAS system with multimedia infotainment application to give deterministic peripheral IO address translation latency of 2 cycles per transaction and system data throughput of 8 GB/s.

title: Gesture-to-Text: A CNN-Based Deep Learning Model for Sign Language Translation
authors: V. S. Manoj Kumar; M. Vara Prasad; R. Landage; V. Golla; R.Reenadevi; G.Thailambal
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Recent Trends in Electrical, Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICRTEECT)
abstract: Hearing and speech impaired people possess the essential communication method through sign language. The availability of sign language communication remains limited because people have insufficient knowledge about this language. This research focuses on the key aspect of Sign Language Translation through CNN-Based Deep Learning since CNNs translate gestures into textual output. The proposed method for sign language evaluation consists of image gathering followed by pattern recognition steps to reach vocabulary level hand gesture identification for sign language processing. Extended datasets of hand gestures enable CNN deep learning models to develop accurate and stable computational results during training. Real-time image processing techniques active in the system build up gesture recognition performance by minimizing recognition errors. Under different lighting and background conditions the CNN model achieves a detection accuracy greater than 95% for sign language gestures. The extraction of features performed by CNNs surpasses traditional machine learning methods by allowing automatic features instead of manual design.

title: Implementation of Data Consistency and Location Traceability in Industrial Development Processes
authors: C. Zhang; J. Cheng; Y. Zhang; S. Chen; S. Zhang; B. An
venue: 2026 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)
abstract: To address the problems of data silos, difficulties in real-time synchronization, and inefficiency in location traceability faced by the equipment development during the digital transformation of the manufacturing industry, this study constructs an industrial R&D process data management system based on an event message monitoring mechanism. The research designs standardized interfaces using a factory-strategy-template model to decouple interfaces from models and integrate multi-source heterogeneous data. Relying on the RabbitMQ message queue, an event monitoring mechanism is built to define data change events, capture and transmit data change information in real time, and achieve data synchronization. Through visual comparison of the model structure tree, accurate locating of data changes and fulllink traceability are realized. Experimental verification shows that the data synchronization delay and location traceability time consumption of this method are both at the second level, the efficiency is significantly improved compared with traditional methods, and it has 100% traceability integrity and strong scalability. This achievement not only provides an efficient and reliable technical solution for the digital transformation of industrial enterprises, but also offers new practical support for the theories of real-time synchronization and location traceability in the field of industrial data management.

title: Network Traffic Analysis for Real-Time Detection of Cyber Attacks
authors: M. Patel; S. R. Prabhu; A. K. Agrawal
venue: 2021 8th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
abstract: Preventing the cyberattacks has been a concern for any organization. In this research, the authors propose a novel method to detect cyberattacks by monitoring and analyzing the network traffic. It was observed that the various log files that are created in the server does not contain all the relevant traces to detect a cyberattack. Hence, the HTTP traffic to the web server was analyzed to detect any potential cyberattacks. To validate the research, a web server was simulated using the Opensource Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) and the cyberattacks were simulated as per the OWASP standards. A python program was scripted that captured the network traffic to the DVWA server. This traffic was analyzed in real-time by reading the various HTTP parameters viz., URLs, Get / Post methods and the dependencies. The results were found to be encouraging as all the simulated attacks in real-time could be successfully detected. This work can be used as a template by various organizations to prevent any insider threat by monitoring the internal HTTP traffic.

title: Generating RSCAD FX Models for Real-Time EMT-Simulation using Component Graphs and PyAPI-RTS
authors: P. Schmurr; N. Liu; A. Schmidt; H. K. Çakmak; A. Kocher; K. Baumgarten; V. Hagenmeyer
venue: 2026 Open Source Modelling and Simulation of Energy Systems (OSMSES)
abstract: The transition of the power grid, driven by the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources and inverter-based resources, necessitates real-time EMT simulations for accurate system representation and stability assessment. However, migrating models to RSCAD FX, the modeling software of RTDS real-time simulators, is non-trivial, and existing solutions are often inflexible. The RSCAD FX version 2.4 has introduced a Python API for controlling simulations and modifying models via program code. However, the API requires manual placement of each electrical and control component individually to determine the correct connectivity of the model elements. In this paper, we introduce an updated version of the PyAPI-RTS open-source software that is now capable of interacting with the official RSCAD Python API and generating or importing models from connectivity information without the need to place the elements manually. To do so, we introduce a novel component graph data structure and a layout algorithm that are described in this paper. The approach is then applied to a small demonstration model and a larger real world use case.

title: Automated Unit Test Generation via Metaprogramming: A Deterministic Alternative to AI-Based Test Synthesis
authors: N. Bhatt
venue: 2025 International Conference on Information, Implementation, and Innovation in Technology (I2ITCON)
abstract: Automated test generation plays a crucial role in modern software development, with AI-driven methods and search-based heuristics being widely explored. However, these approaches often suffer from incomplete test coverage, nondeterministic behavior, and high computational costs. This paper introduces a novel metaprogramming-based technique for automatically generating unit tests from integration tests in Python. By leveraging function metadata at runtime, the approach extracts meaningful test cases without requiring manual test design or AI-driven synthesis. Unlike generative AI, which relies on probabilistic models, the method ensures deterministic and reproducible test generation. Experimental results demonstrate that the approach maintains high code coverage while significantly reducing the overhead associated with traditional test generation techniques. This work presents a practical and efficient alternative for developers seeking reliable automated testing without the uncertainty of AI-based solutions.

title: Real Time Traffic Sign Recognition Model Using Convolutional Neural Network
authors: M. Kandasamy; R. Shanmugam; P. Harikrishna; K. A. P; A. Francis; K. Arora
venue: 2023 International Conference on Computer Science and Emerging Technologies (CSET)
abstract: This paper aims to summarise the development of a robust and accurate system for detecting traffic signs in real-time using convolutional neural networks (CNN) and the Python programming language. By enabling autonomous vehicles to reliably identify and interpret traffic signs, the goal is to increase road safety. The proposed method seeks to handle difficulties brought on by real-world settings, such as fluctuating lighting, weather, and obstructions, by developing an efficient pre-processing method and using a CNN-based model for feature extraction and classification. The goal is to achieve high accuracy in traffic sign detection while maintaining real-time performance, making it a feasible solution for autonomous driving systems.

title: Design and Implementation of Web Real-time Alarm System Based on Push Technology
authors: X. Zhang; Y. Chen; Q. Zou; M. Hou
venue: 2022 9th International Forum on Electrical Engineering and Automation (IFEEA)
abstract: In order to meet the real-time requirements of the alarm system in the power system, this paper focuses on the use of the push framework Pushlet[1] to realize the real-time push of server alarm data, and designs and implements a web real-time alarm system. The web real-time alarm system based on push technology has the advantages of less page requests, less alarm delay, and moderate communication flow. It provides a solution for the application of real-time monitoring on the web. The system has been widely used in power system projects.

title: FPGA-Accelerated Video Watermarking Using Python and Verilog on Zynq SoC
authors: J. P. Singh Tomar; A. Chaturvedi; M. Kumar
venue: 2025 IEEE Silchar Subsection Conference (SILCON)
abstract: This article presents an innovative video watermarking technique that’s been implemented on the Xilinx Zynq System-on-Chip (SoC). Nevertheless, the method cleverly splits the workload: the ARM Cortex-A9 processor takes care of the high-level video tasks using Python and OpenCV, while custom Verilog logic on the FPGA efficiently embeds a strong watermark into the luminance (Y) channel of the video frame. By utilizing AXI interfaces for communication, this hybrid system delivers well real-time performance and watermark durability compare to traditional software-only methods.

title: Sign Language To Speech Translation
authors: N. P. Samuel; P. Vishnu Samy Jayavel; S. Ancy
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Future Innovations (ETFI)
abstract: Sign Language is the important means of communication for the people with speech and hearing aid, but still it is not accessible by majority of the population because it lacks the interpretation in everyday conversation. This study presents a real time sign-language translator that combines the Computer Vision and the Deep Learning concepts to reduce this gap. The architecture combines MediaPipe-based hand tracking with a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) architecture to perform feature representation and learning of gesture sequences. Preprocessed video frames will be captured by the webcam and this frames will be given to the model to predict the whole sentence instead of the single alphabet letters. The generated output will be given in the format of converted text and will be given to the Text-to-Speech model, so that we can also have Speech as a output. Experimental testing verifies that the suggested technique is able to process dynamic sequences of gestures, thus enhancing natural sign-to-sentence translation over conventional static models. This research advances the development of an intelligent real-time aid system improving hearing-impaired inclusiveness.

title: Design and Implementation of Underwater Acoustic Signal Acquisition and Display Software Based on PyQt5
authors: C. Li; Y. Huang; S. Liu; L. Yue; B. Liu
venue: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In underwater target detection experiments, real-time signal processing and result display of collected underwater acoustic signal data are very important for the experiment. This paper has designed and implemented an underwater acoustic signal acquisition and display software based on PyQt5. This software can control the acquisition device to collect real-time underwater acoustic signal data received by active sonar, and perform relevant signal processing and result display on the data in real time. This software uses a serial port to achieve communication between the software and the acquisition device. It controls the acquisition device by calling the C++ dynamic link library provided by the acquisition device developer. The software obtains real-time underwater acoustic signal data from the acquisition device, and then performs relevant signal processing on the underwater acoustic signal data. The data processing results are displayed in the form of time-domain graphs, spectrograms, and target trajectory graphs. During the experiment, users can also save the experiment data in real time as needed, and replay these experiment data files as needed after the experiment. Through extensive practical testing, this paper has demonstrated that the software effectively achieves real-time acquisition, signal processing, and result display of underwater acoustic signals. It has the advantages of low code volume, high execution efficiency, strong stability, and good scalability.

title: Towards real-time scheduling of virtual machines without kernel modifications
authors: M. Åsberg; N. Forsberg; T. Nolte; S. Kato
venue: ETFA2011
abstract: Virtualization is a well used technique in the area of internet server systems for managing several (legacy) applications on a single physical machine. These applications do not have strict time deadlines, which also reflects how these applications are scheduled. Using virtualization in an embedded real-time systems context is of course attractive, since we want to pack as much software as possible on a, as small as possible, hardware platform. The problem is that this kind of software does not easily cope well together, in the aspect of time related properties. Hence, we need a new mechanism, i.e., a scheduler, that can satisfy the timing requirements of each application. However, scheduler implementations typically require modifications to middleware or kernel and this is not acceptable in the area embedded systems, due to stability and reliability reasons. Hence, in this paper, we propose a framework for scheduling (soft real-time) applications residing in separate operating systems (virtual machines) using hierarchical fixed-priority preemptive scheduling, without the requirement of kernel modifications.1

title: Development of the Address in Real Time (ART) Data Driver Card (ADDC) test procedures of the New Small Wheel upgrade project
authors: D. Matakias; L. Yao; G. Iakovidis; T. Alexopoulos
venue: 2018 7th International Conference on Modern Circuits and Systems Technologies (MOCAST)
abstract: The upgrades of the LHC accelerator will increase the instantaneous and the integrated luminosity during the data taking in 2019/20 and 2023/24, thus causing increased data and trigger rates. In order to cope with the increased muon rate while maintaining high muon detection efficiency the current ATLAS small wheel muon detectors will be replaced with a New Small Wheel (NSW) for high luminosity LHC runs. The NSW will feature two new detector technologies: resistive MicroMegas and small strip Thin Gap Chambers with a total of 2.4 million readout channels. The MicroMegas and TGCs will have common readout paths but separate trigger paths. For the MicroMegas detector, the trigger primitive is the Address in Real Time (ART) signal. The ART Data Driver Card (ADDC) is designed for the MicroMegas detector to process and transmit the trigger data from the front end ASICs to the trigger processor. The ADDC will be located on the detector alongside the front-end electronics, while the trigger processor will be placed away from the high radiation and magnetic field environment. Therefore, it is crucial to thoroughly test the ADDC, since access will be difficult and limited once the NSW is installed. In order to perform a realistic test a dedicated firmware has been developed for the VC707 evaluation card, capable of generating ART signals and reading the ADDC card response that is send to the trigger processor. The FPGA can validate the ADDC response in real time and signify any errors found. A software library has also been developed, in order to control and monitor the test setup using a computer. Finally, a user interface will be developed to simplify and automate the test process.

title: Real-Time DDoS Detection Using XGBoost and Streaming Analytics
authors: G. K. K; C. K; G. S S; M. V
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Emerging Research in Electronics, Computer Science and Technology (ICERECT)
abstract: Traditional security systems are ineffective at detecting and mitigating DDoS attacks in real time due to the growth of DDoS attacks exploit the high volume and complexity of modern network traffic, aiming to disrupt system availability by overwhelming targets with excessive data flow. Here, we propose a DDoS detection system that works in real time using the machine learning algorithm XGBoost with Python libraries. Scapy captures live network packets, Apache Kafka handles real-time data streaming, supported by several preprocessing modules for data cleaning and feature extraction. After tuning parameters, the model trained on CICDDoS2019 detects DDoS attacks with an accuracy of 99.97%. The system classifies malicious traffic very efficiently and also supports visualization techniques to monitor traffic behavior and patterns. This framework forms a commercially practical solution to proactive DDoS detection and can be merged into modern network security infrastructures.

title: UBER: An Unreal Engine Based Simulation Platform with Extensibility and Real-time Capability*
authors: J. Chen; Z. Shi; X. Wang; J. Wu
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Real-time Computing and Robotics (RCAR)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a real-time platform called UBER, which stands for Unreal Engine Based simulation platform with Extensibility and Real-time capability. It provides a visualization way to the online tests of unmanned vehicle simulation with Unreal Engine 5 (UE5). By building a TCP communication module to exchange message between two ends in UBER, we successfully solve the problem that no code script can be operated in blueprints of UE5. Excellent physics components in UE5 makes simulation visualization more real and beautiful compared with other Reinforcement Learning environments, and by accessing the python scripts outside of blueprints, various of elements, such as scenario components and environmental settings, etc., can be easily modified. Furthermore, a series of reinforcement learning and formation control algorithms are implemented on UBER to show its extensibility and real-time capability, proving that our TCP communication method brings forth a good solution to the problem that UE5 does not support python scripts within blueprint.

title: UDS: A Unified Approach to Deterministic Multithreading
authors: F. J. Hauck; J. Domaschka
venue: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems (ICDCS)
abstract: There are several applications for the deterministic execution of software, e.g. replicated systems, test and febugging scenarios. In all cases the execution should lead zo the same effects in order to be consistent. Multi-threading is one of the major sources of nondeterminism. Several deterministic scheduling algorithms exist that allow concurrent but deterministic executions despite of arbitrary switching decisions of the underlying system schedulers. We present the novel and flexible Unified Deterministic Scheduling algorithm (UDS) for weakly and fully deterministic systems. Compared to existing algorithms, UDS has a broad parameter set that can be (re-)configured even at runtime. Further, we show that many existing algorithms are merely a particular configuration of UDS.

title: Smart Traffic Intersection Management System for Efficient Urban Mobility
authors: A. K. C. S; L. B. S; V. V. B; K. Arun Kumar; V. G. K
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on New Frontiers in Communication, Automation, Management and Security (ICCAMS)
abstract: This project presents a hybrid traffic management system integrating Python-based image processing and Verilog-based traffic signal control through socket-based communication. The system utilizes real-time traffic data, process vehicle density, and detect violations such as red-light crossing and overspeeding. The extracted data is transmitted to an FPGA-based traffic controller, which dynamically adjusts signal timings to optimize traffic flow. The real-time adaptability of the system enhances traffic efficiency, minimizes congestion, and improves road safety, making it a scalable solution for smart city applications.

title: Implementation and Analysis of a Generator Health Index Model Based on Condition Assessment Data at Coal-Fired Power Plant
authors: E. A. Gumilar; V. Refikhanata; B. Denov; U. Khayam
venue: 2024 6th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Generators are essential for power generation, enabling energy production and distribution. Disruptions in generator operation can cause significant issues and economic losses. Current maintenance practices, which involve testing individual subsystems, do not provide a comprehensive overview of the generator’s overall health. This limitation makes early detection of issues challenging and increases the risk of unexpected failures. This research aims to develop a Generator Health Index (GHI) model that integrates condition assessment data with operational maintenance data to provide real-time insights into generator health. The GHI model is created using a scoring and weighting method with various sub-components based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), contributing to the overall generator condition as part of the condition assessment framework. Scores are assigned based on criteria values aligned with relevant standards, and the weight of each component and parameter is determined by assessing its relative impact on the overall generator condition. This paper focuses on implementing the GHI at the Indramayu, West Java, Indonesia 2 unit from the 3 x 330 MW coal-fired power plant, addressing how the data is handled, including instances where data was not collected in certain years, and evaluating the quality of the data. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in real-time decision-making and maintenance planning at the Indramayu, West Java, Indonesia Coal-Fired Power Plant, reducing the risk of unexpected failures.

title: HIL Testbed-based Auto Feature Extraction and Data Generation Framework for ML/DL-based Anomaly Detection and Classification
authors: A. A. Mantha; A. Hussain; G. Ravikumar
venue: 2024 IEEE Power & Energy Society Innovative Smart Grid Technologies Conference (ISGT)
abstract: In smart grid operations, sufficient data generation, including events such as faults, cyberattacks, and perturbations, is one of the key requirements for accurate Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) based anomaly detection and classification. However, the public datasets in power systems pose data sufficiency, bias, and uncertainty challenges. Moreover, synthetic datasets may only capture some feature vectors in power systems and complex dynamics, resulting in sub-optimal performance of ML/DL models. In this paper, we proposed the Auto Feature Extraction and Data Generation (AFEDG) framework for ML and DL models in smart grid applications such as anomaly detection and classification. We developed a Python-based Application Programming Interface (API) to automate the extraction of feature vectors and data generation processes by integrating virtual sensors. The API dynamically modulates parameters and signals within the power system model, ensuring comprehensive coverage of all event scenarios and generating unbiased, balanced datasets. The proposed API is designed to seamlessly integrate with power systems, exhibiting scalability and adaptability regardless of the number of buses within the system. We implemented the proposed AFEDG framework on a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Cyber-Physical System (CPS) testbed to generate large-scale real-time datasets. In our case study, we used the Python API to generate electric fault datasets on the modified SSN-distribution bus grid model in OPAL-RT, integrating with RT-LAB and MATLAB.

title: Web-based monitoring alarm system for low-voltage distribution network
authors: Y. Song; K. Zhu
venue: 2023 2nd International Conference on Cloud Computing, Big Data Application and Software Engineering (CBASE)
abstract: Distribution network monitoring is an important part of the Distribution Automation system, Web real-time monitoring system is to reflect the operating conditions of the actual power system, and it needs real-time processing and maintenance for large amounts of data. The traditional C/S mode of distribution system, with the gradual modernization of the distribution system, shows their flaws. Traditional centralized C/S mode of distribution automation systems is changed to distributed B/S mode. The system uses JSP pages technology and new Ajax technology to improve the existing distribution automation of B/S mode monitoring software platform, to achieve real-time monitoring of alarms of distribution network, alarm history record check and other common features of the power monitoring system, to enhance grid monitoring automation management.

title: Ai-Based Sign Language to Text Translator Using Computer Vision and Deep Learning
authors: P. Iyer; M. Nguyen; N. Everett; O. Primitivo; G. Collins; M. Hajiarbabi
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Data Intelligence and Cognitive Informatics (ICDICI)
abstract: Over half a million people in the United States use American Sign Language (ASL), yet only a fraction of the general population understands it, creating significant communication barriers. This paper introduces an innovative, real time American Sign Language Translation system, designed to bridge those communication barriers between ASL users and non-signers. Integrating computer vision (CV), deep learning, and natural language processing (NLP), we successfully can capture, recognize, and translate ASL movements into coherent textual output. Landmark training extraction and spatial-temporal modeling with hybrid architectures led to the team conceptualizing a unique combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM). Additionally, recognizing ASL's contextual nature [15], Large Language Models (LLM) trained with NLP are used to reason out sentences. Extensive evaluation demonstrated a $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$ average accuracy in gesture classification, robust performance under varied environmental conditions (lighting, hand sizes, gesture speed), and real time applicability. This research highlights the urgent need for improved accessibility standards, empowering ASL users toward greater independence. Future work could further integrate this technology into broadcast media, enhance gesture recognition speed, and extend translations to additional sign languages.

title: Communication System for the Deaf and Mute
authors: D. Lingineni; P. DRL; R. K. Addanki; S. Singarapu; J. B. Reddy
venue: 2026 Fourth International Conference on Augmented Intelligence and Sustainable Systems (ICAISS)
abstract: The paper proposes a new and efficient full-duplex communication system that fills the gap between Deaf and Mute (D-M) and Non-Deaf and Mute (ND-M) people without the need for ND-M people to learn sign language. In contrast to other models that only support unidirectional translation or translation in a single language, this system allows for real-time bidirectional translation in multiple sign languages, namely Indian Sign Language (ISL) and American Sign Language (ASL). The system also supports Speech-to-ISL/ASL, Text-to-ISL/ASL, ASL- to-ISL, and ASL-to-Speech translation. The system is developed using Machine Learning (ML), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to provide high accuracy in gesture recognition and context-aware translation. The system is cost-effective, scalable, and can be applied in various settings such as education, healthcare, and public service sectors. The system is modular and can be easily extended to incorporate other sign languages. Experimental evaluations show over 96% accuracy with real-time responsiveness. The system and codebase are openly available to encourage replicability and wider adoption, thereby promoting digital inclusivity for the D-M community. Future enhancements include dataset expansion, full-word recognition, and collaborative deployment with accessibility-focused organizations.

title: Region-based memory management for real-time Java
authors: T. Higuera; V. Issarny; M. Banatre; G. Cabillic; J. . -P. Lesot; F. Parain
venue: Fourth IEEE International Symposium on Object-Oriented Real-Time Distributed Computing. ISORC 2001
abstract: The paper addresses the issue of improving the performance of memory management for real time Java applications, building upon the Real-Time Specification for Java (RTSJ) from the Real-Time Java Expert Group. In a first step, a thorough analysis of the parameters influencing the performance of memory management together with ways of improvement are presented. The implementation of a memory management solution, which is compliant with the RTSJ and integrating the proposed improvements is then sketched.

title: Real-time event kernel architecture for home-network gateway set-top-box (HNGS)
authors: Jae-Chul Moon; Hyo-Sang Lim; Soon-Ju Kang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper discusses a software architecture for a set-top-box that serves as intermediary connecting home networks to the Internet. As the major design challenge in developing the software is supporting inherent real-time requirements of home networks and home Internet connectivity simultaneously, the software is designed to integrate both real-time service and home Internet connectivity into one software framework.

title: The Komodo project: thread-based event handling supported by a multithreaded Java microcontroller
authors: J. Kreuzinger; R. Marston; T. Ungerer; U. Brinkschulte; C. Krakowski
venue: Proceedings 25th EUROMICRO Conference. Informatics: Theory and Practice for the New Millennium
abstract: The Komodo project concerns the handling of multiple real-time events by Java threads that are supported by a multithreaded Java microcontroller. The architecture of the processor core and resulting implications are considered. The use of thread-based event handling is introduced and explained in combination with an Automatic Guided Vehicle (AGV) application. The advantages of thread-based event handling over a normal Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) strategy are demonstrated by the development of the AGV example.

title: Real-Time Multimodal Speech and Sign Language Translation System with Semantic and Intent Analysis Using YOLOv5
authors: K. Kamal; Y. Mishra; K. Dhivya
venue: 2026 International Conference on Recent Advances in Electrical, Electronics, Ubiquitous Communication, and Computational Intelligence (RAEEUCCI)
abstract: Communication between spoken and sign language users is challenging, which this model addresses through realtime multimodal interaction. It uses YOLOv5 for hand gesture recognition and Whisper for multilingual speech-to-text, enabling understanding of both sign and spoken inputs. The system translates gestures into text, interprets speech, and generates appropriate responses, including synthesized voice output. Its performance is evaluated using Precision, Recall, IoU, and mAP, and it provides a lightweight, scalable solution for accessible communication for individuals with hearing and speech disabilities.

title: Real – Time Communication System for Specially Abled Powered by AI
authors: T. Poornachandar; T. Sathieskumar; K. Thangadurai; M. Dinesh Kumar; V. Anuradha; T. Jayasri
venue: 2025 International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (ICCCT)
abstract: Our project primarily focuses on developing a model to facilitate communication for deaf or dumb individuals, who often face significant challenges in interacting with others. Real-time communication is a critical aspect of life, enabling individuals to connect instantly from anywhere globally. Our system aims to recognize hand gestures, text and speech. It perform tasks such as Sign Language convert into text and speech and the text will be convert into speech with our desired language, ensuring it is received within the appropriate hearing frequency range. To achieve this, the proposed system will incorporate artificial intelligence by creating a model using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize Indian Sign Language or human actions and convert them into text and audio formats. The corresponding messages will be sent via Global System for Mobile Communication (GSM) module to the wearer's Android device, which will convert the text into speech. By utilizing an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), and Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) algorithm, facilitate multilingual speech translation. By using Real-time Protocol (RTP) for recording functions for the future use. This AI-Powered system also establishes speech and text processing via Bluetooth-enabled mobile connectivity for seamless interaction.

title: A Web-Based Framework for Real-Time Sign Language Translation: Integrating Gesture and Speech for Enhanced Accessibility
authors: A. R. Borah; Pramila.S; S. Mondal; V. Vidyarthy; A. A. Burhan; N. Singhal
venue: 2025 International Conference on Computing Technologies (ICOCT)
abstract: Sign language translation technologies have become essential in promoting inclusivity and enabling communication for the specially abled community. This paper presents a comparative study of existing translation techniques, including computer vision, wearable sensors, and natural language processing-based systems. We evaluate these methodologies based on key metrics such as accuracy, latency, accessibility, and real-world applicability. Our findings highlight the trade-offs between these approaches, with wearable sensors providing higher accuracy and lower latency, while computer vision-based methods excel in accessibility. The study emphasizes the need for hybrid solutions that combine the strengths of multiple approaches to achieve both technical robustness and user-centric accessibility.

title: Real-Time BIM–IoT Synchronization for Operational Digital Twins: The HPC4AI Data Center Case Study
authors: V. Vaccaro; L. C. Tagliabue; R. Birke
venue: 2026 34th Euromicro International Conference on Parallel, Distributed, and Network-Based Processing (PDP)
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are emerging as a key enabling technology for the operational management of mission-critical infrastructures, where real-time integration between physical systems, Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring, and Building Information Modelling (BIM) can support optimization, predictive control, and sustainability. In this context, the University of Turin's Computer Science Department is developing a DT of its HPC4AI data center, aimed at improving environmental monitoring, operational awareness, and energy-efficient management. The BIM model, originally generated from as-built documentation, was enriched to act as the geometric and semantic backbone of the DT. To create a live connection with the physical infrastructure, rack-level probes and environmental sensors are linked to BIM elements through dedicated shared parameters; this mapping is operationalized through a workflow based on Dynamo and custom Python scripts, which inject time-series measurements into the model as dynamic operational attributes rather than static annotations. Sensors inject timestamped measurements into a timeseries DB based on InfluxDB. Python scripts embedded in Dynamo periodically query InfluxDB via authenticated HTTP requests, parse the retrieved JSON data, and update the corresponding Revit parameters in real time, transforming the BIM model from a static geometric repository into a dynamic information system capable of reflecting the actual operational state of the data center. This process enables the representation of the current microclimatic state directly within the BIM environment. A dedicated alert engine evaluates incoming values against predefined thresholds and generates diagnostic flags and historical alert records. Graphical overrides highlight critical sensors through colour-coded states, allowing immediate spatial localization of anomalies. The methodology follows recent research trends demonstrating that BIM–IoT integration is essential for Facility Management-oriented DTs, enabling buildings to evolve into continuously updated, data-driven systems rather than fixed models. The paper discusses the system architecture, data synchronization strategy, and scalability for integrating additional sensors and control loops. Preliminary results show that the BIM–IoT bridge enhances situational awareness and lays the groundwork for predictive control and energy optimization of the data center infrastructure.

title: Memory dump and forensic analysis based on virtual machine
authors: L. Guangqi; W. Lianhai; Z. Shuhui; X. Shujiang; Z. Lei
venue: 2014 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation
abstract: A memory dump and forensic analysis algorithm is proposed based on virtual machine in the paper, including the virtual machine process search module, virtual machine memory dump module and virtual machine memory forensics analysis modules. First of all, the virtual machine process search module by traversal searching all the running processes in system, according to the process owner user to identify the process of the virtual machine. And then, using the virtual machine memory dump module to dump the memory of the virtual machine process and the memory files is occupied. Finally, using the memory forensics analysis module to analyze accessed memory files, obtain evidence of the virtual machine information, such as process information, network information, user information, etc. This method can neither rewriting memory of the virtual machine and the system, ensure the integrity and efficiency of the virtual machine memory and forensic analysis, at the same time the dump memory files can be repeated analysis, guarantee the credibility of forensic results.

title: IoT-Enabled GNSS-based System for Real-Time Ionospheric Scintillation Monitoring
authors: H. V. Vankayala; A. Mahadevan; S. S. Kongani; A. S. Reddy; V. R. Devanaboyina
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning depends on the integrity of signals traversing the ionosphere. However, ionospheric irregularities can induce rapid fluctuations in signal amplitude and phase, known as scintillations, which degrade positioning accuracy and reliability. Traditional ionospheric scintillation monitors are often expensive and fixed in location, limiting widespread monitoring and real-time analysis. To address this, we propose an IoT-enabled, low-cost GNSS-based prototype for monitoring ionospheric amplitude scintillations. The system leverages IoT technologies, integrating off-the-shelf GNSS receivers with real-time data transmission capabilities to compute the S4 index—a critical parameter for quantifying amplitude scintillations for all the visible satellites. The processed S4 data is automatically uploaded to a cloud database, eliminating the need for manual interaction with the system. A web-based dashboard provides remote access to the data, allowing multiple users to visualize real-time scintillation activity from anywhere, ensuring seamless monitoring and analysis. Leveraging IoT technology, this portable and scalable system surpasses traditional monitoring methods by enabling seamless, real-time ionospheric observation. Its integration of cloud-based data storage, remote accessibility, and automated processing ensures continuous, hands-free monitoring, to improve the reliability of GNSS-based navigation in dynamic ionospheric conditions.

title: Multilingual Hand Gesture Recognition for Deaf and Dumb People Using NLP and CV
authors: B. Renukadevi; V. Sarveshwaran; T. A. P; K. S; R. R
venue: 2025 International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (ICCCT)
abstract: A Multilingual Hand Gesture Recognition for Deaf and Dumb people using NLP and CV is a technology that converts sign language gestures into spoken language or text and vice versa, facilitating communication between sign language users and non-users. Our project aims to transform real-time communication by translating hand gestures into multiple languages and providing humanized text during video calls. Index Terms- Sign Language Translation, Real-Time Communication, Hand Gesture Recognition, Multilingual Translation, Natural Language Processing(NLP), Gesture-to- Text Conversion.

title: Indian Sign Language Recognition and Translation into Regional Language for Hearing and Speech Impaired Bedridden People
authors: P. P. Raj; A. Gokhale; V. S. Gutte; M. S.D.
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Trends and Innovations in ICT (ICEI)
abstract: This research paper presents a system for real-time Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition and translation, designed to assist hospitalized or bedridden deaf and mute individuals in communicating with healthcare providers and caretakers. Utilizing MediaPipe for hand landmark detection and OpenCV for video capture, the system identifies emergency-related gestures, translating them into English, Hindi, and Marathi. A Random Forest Classifier is employed to classify signs, enabling accurate gesture recognition under varying conditions. The system addresses key technical challenges, including real-time gesture detection, feature normalization, and handling missing landmarks. Futhermore, the system was tested in real-world scenarios, resulting in excellent outcomes. By reducing reliance on human translators, this solution empowers deaf and mute individuals to communicate more effectively, enhancing their autonomy and inclusivity in healthcare environments. The proposed system offers a promising approach for bridging communication gaps, improving emergency response, and fostering greater inclusivity for the hearing and speech-impaired community, particularly in healthcare settings.

title: Efficient and Reliable Clustering by Parallel Random Swap Algorithm
authors: L. Nigro; F. Cicirelli; P. Fränti
venue: 2022 IEEE/ACM 26th International Symposium on Distributed Simulation and Real Time Applications (DS-RT)
abstract: Solving large-scale clustering problems requires an efficient algorithm which can be implemented also in parallel. K-means would be suitable but it can lead to an inaccurate clustering result. To overcome this problem, we present a parallel version of random swap clustering algorithm. It combines the scalability of k-means with high clustering accuracy. The new clustering method is experimented on top of Java parallel streams and lambda expressions, which offer interesting execution time benefits. The method is applied to standard benchmark datasets, with a varying population size and distribution of managed records, dimensionality of data points and the number of clusters. The experimental results confirm that high quality clustering can be obtained by parallel random swap together with a high time efficiency.

title: Real-time performance of energy based underwater acoustic event detectors embedded in a single-board computer
authors: A. Alvarez-Rosario; L. R. Padovese
venue: 2015 IEEE/OES Acoustics in Underwater Geosciences Symposium (RIO Acoustics)
abstract: Summation of energy, commonly known as Energy Detectors, is a class of signal processing methods that can be used to detect underwater acoustic events in the recorded signal data. The key in Energy Detectors is the construction of a Detection Function that can differentiate the acoustic event from the background. In this work, we evaluate the performance of some classical approaches that develop detection functions based on energy summation, as well as their performance when running in a single-board computer for real-time analysis. A set of underwater acoustic recordings (pcm wave files) containing some bioacoustics events, with different size and frequency sampling, were used to construct signals envelopes. In each case, a set of methods (root mean square, moving average, absolute square value, fast Fourier transform and Hilbert transform) with different parameters values (window size and overlap) were tested on a Raspberry PI B+ (RPI) using Python as programming language. Results shows that RPI is able to perform post-processing tasks to construct the detection functions of the recorded signals, while acquiring data at the same time. This characteristic demonstrates their potential in developing real time detection systems on single board computers as RPI.

title: Development and Implementation of Real-Time Biological Image Recognition System Based on You Look Only Once Algorithm
authors: S. -W. Lin; W. -K. Hsieh; Y. -S. Liu; J. -M. Zhang; H. -Z. Zhou
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Computation, Big-Data and Engineering (ICCBE)
abstract: We developed a real-time biological image recognition system based on the YOLOv8 algorithm for rapid and accurate identification of animals. The model was trained using augmented datasets, generated using Roboflow with grayscale conversion, blurring, and flipping, on the Google Colaboratory platform. A lightweight Python-Based application was developed using Kivy and KivyMD frameworks to implement the trained model. The model supports static image and real-time camera input, features bilingual (Chinese/English) labels, and integrates Wikipedia query functionality. It operates offline and runs smoothly on standard laptops or mobile devices without requiring high-end hardware. With an intuitive user interface, the model is accessible to general users, including students and educators. The developed model demonstrates strong practical value and extensibility, making it well-suited for ecological education, outdoor fieldwork, and mobile learning. Future improvements are necessary to include expanded species support and integration of additional educational content.

title: A Novel Framework for Automatic Generation of Dynamic Visualizations from Python Code in Data Analysis
authors: V. M; V. M; D. K; M. S. H. P; S. G. R. M
venue: 2025 IEEE First International Conference on Innovations in Engineering and Next-Generation Technologies for Sustainability (ICINVENTS)
abstract: Existing data visualization tools predominantly rely on manual development or traditional software solutions to translate raw data into meaningful visual representations. However, these methods often lack efficiency and fail to provide an intuitive way to generate visualizations directly from high-level code. To overcome these challenges, we propose developing a framework for automatic visualization generation from Python code for data analysis applications. This framework translates Python code into dynamic visualizations by interpreting the logic and data structures, enabling seamless design and execution. By leveraging advanced visualization techniques, the system ensures efficient and accurate representation of complex datasets, enhancing the usability of data analysis tools. The solution includes real-time code interpretation, allowing for immediate visualization generation and interaction. A secure cloudbased platform supports the storage and execution of generated visualizations while ensuring compliance with computational and data privacy standards. Additionally, an intuitive interface provides actionable insights, including performance metrics, visualization customization options, and interaction capabilities. The system integrates seamlessly with existing data science frameworks and ensures data security through encryption and role-based access control. Furthermore, the innovation supports modular and scalable design, enabling researchers and developers to adapt visualizations for evolving analytical needs.

title: Vision Transformers-Powered Classroom Engagement Monitoring System for Real-Time Insights
authors: R. R; M. Palav; I. Zeeshan; H. Azra; M. A. R. K. T; N. R. Joshi
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Recent Trends in Computer Science and Technology (ICRTCST)
abstract: The paper is a vision transformers-based classroom engagement monitoring mechanism that is expected to deliver real-time and consistent information regarding the level of attention of students. The suggested method utilizes the Adaptive Histogram Equalization (AHE) technique as a preprocessing method to improve the quality of visuals in different illumination conditions in order to assure the same features are extracted. The Vision Transformer self-attention maps are used to perform automatic feature selection so that the model could pay attention to the most pertinent facial, pose, and contextual features related to engagement behavior. H-ViT classifier is a classifier that combines these cues to provide high-quality engagement predictions, which are more accurate than standard CNN and LSTM-based models. The system has been implemented in Python and PyTorch and shows great real-time, interpretability, and works well in the complex classroom setting. The results show that the suggested framework offers a scalable and effective approach to intelligent learning analytics, which can be used to support the strategic use of data to teach according to the needs of the intended audience and enhance the overall interaction analysis of the classroom.

title: Tech for Inclusivity: A Universal Communication Device for Diverse Expression
authors: S. S; T. A; A. S; H. V; A. R
venue: 2025 International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (ICCCT)
abstract: Effective communication is essential for social integration, yet individuals who rely on sign language often face barriers when interacting with those unfamiliar with it. This research presents a dual-purpose system to facilitate seamless communication. The first module employs Computer Vision and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize sign language gestures and convert them into text and speech in real time. The second module utilizes Speech Recognition, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Neural Machine Translation (NMT) to transcribe spoken language and translate it into the user's preferred language. The system is accessible across various platforms, ensuring ease of use for a wide range of users. Through the integration of various technologies, this approach seeks to promote social fairness and inclusivity by bridging the communication gap between the general public and those who use sign language.

title: American Sign Language Translation with Emotion Recognition
authors: M. V; N. N; R. M
venue: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference for Advancement in Technology (ICONAT)
abstract: This project focuses on the development of a system that integrates American Sign Language (ASL) translation with emotion recognition, aiming to enhance communication for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community. The system takes advan- tage of advanced machine learning techniques and computer vision to accurately interpret ASL gestures and facial expressions. By incorporating emotion recognition, the project adds a layer of context, enabling the system to better capture the emotional details of communication, thus improving its effectiveness and empathy. The solution utilizes a multi-modal approach that uses deep learning algorithms for gesture recognition and sentiment analysis. Video feeds are processed to identify hand gestures, body movements, and facial expressions, translating them into text. Emotion recognition algorithms analyze facial expressions to detect emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, or surprise, enhancing the translation with emotional context. The system is designed with a focus on scalability, real-time processing, and user friendly, offering potential applications in education, customer service, and accessibility technologies. This project not only bridges the gap between American Sign Language (ASL) users and non-ASL users, but also sets a foundation for more inclusive and emotionally intelligent communication systems. Experimental results show the system's accuracy and reliability, emphasizing its feasibility for real-world usage.

title: Real-Time Processing of Common Sign Language using PP-YOLOE Deep Learning Monitoring
authors: S. Devadoss.D; M. N. Krishanan; M. R. Joel
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
abstract: Deaf people and Hard-of-Hearing individuals face communication challenges which create barriers that prevent them from developing social connections and building professional careers and accessing essential services. People have turned to deep learning based assistive technologies which include artificial intelligence (AI) to solve this accessibility problem. The research presents an accessibility solution which enables interpreter services through deep learning technology and keypoint tracking to achieve better inclusion outcomes. The system achieves real-time identification of British Sign Language (BSL) alphabet letters through the combination of PP-YOLOE motion detection model and advanced hand tracking technology. The proposed method deals with three main challenges which include improving computing efficiency and handling environmental changes and resolving gesture recognition difficulties. The PP-YOLOE system achieves an 85% accuracy rate and 87% precision rate which outperforms all other algorithms when evaluated on BSL datasets.

title: Enhancing Wildlife Monitoring: Real-Time Alerts Through Email and Messaging
authors: K. Vidhya; R. C. F; N. B; T. M. Thiyagu; J. Archpaul; C. P. Shirley
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
abstract: Wildlife conservation faces increasing challenges due to habitat encroachment and human-wildlife conflicts. Ensuring real-time detection of wildlife near human settlements is crucial for protecting both animal and human lives. Traditional wildlife monitoring techniques, such as manual patrolling and fixed camera traps, often suffer from delayed response times and limited coverage. These limitations restrict the ability to implement proactive intervention strategies effectively. Conventional methods primarily rely on human observation or cloud-based object detection models, leading to high operational costs and latency issues, especially in remote environments. This work presents a real-time wildlife detection system based on the YOLOv11 model, integrated with automated SMS and email alert mechanisms. The system operates on an edge device, minimizing dependency on cloud infrastructure and ensuring low-latency performance. Simulation experiments were conducted using a dataset comprising 6,993 wildlife images representing elephants, boars, monkeys, and humans under varying conditions. The detection model was evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, and mean Average Precision (mAP) metrics. The system was developed using Python with TensorFlow, OpenCV, and Twilio-Gmail APIs for real-time processing and communication. Experimental results demonstrated a mAP of 81.6% at an IoU threshold of 0.5, precision up to 86%, recall up to 75%, and an alert generation time of less than 0.5 seconds with a 98% delivery success rate. In conclusion, the proposed approach offers a robust, real-time, and scalable solution for wildlife monitoring, significantly improving response times and enhancing the effectiveness of conservation efforts.

title: Computer Vision-Integrated Checkout Automation Framework for Seamless Commerce Operations
authors: C. Bisaria; S. H. I. Gardez; B. S; A. Yadav; Revanayya; A. Sharma; J. Bino
venue: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
abstract: The increased need to make retail operation quicker and more efficient has been an impetus to the creation of smart checkout automation systems. The study suggests a Computer Vision-Based Checkout Automation Framework, which takes advantage of the latest image processing and deep learning algorithms to allow smooth commerce processes. The framework uses Adaptive Histogram Equalization (AHE) as a preprocessing technique to improve the image contrast and overcome the problems associated with different lighting conditions. The most relevant features are determined using Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (RFECV) as it is more cost-effective and the model is more precise. Vision Transformer (ViT) classifier is applied to ensure high-quality recognition of the product even in those cases when it is occluded, overlaps with other objects, or is similar to another product. Python and PyTorch are used to create the system, which may be used in real-time processing and touch-free checkouts. Through experimental simulations, it is shown that the proposed framework is statistically better than the methods which are based on traditional CNN, rule-based, and barcode/RFID in both accuracy, latency and adaptability. The proposed research creates a scalable, efficient, and smart remedy to the contemporary retail automation.

title: pyNeurode: a real-time neural signal processing framework
authors: W. -K. Tam; M. F. Nolan
venue: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Accurate decoding of neural signals often requires assigning extracellular waveforms acquired on the same electrode to their originating neurons, a process known as spike sorting. While many offline sorters are available, accurate online sorting of spikes with many channels is still a challenging problem. Existing online sorters either use simple algorithms with low accuracy, can only process a handful of channels, or depend on a complex runtime environment that is difficult to set up. We have developed a state-of-the-art online spike sorting platform in Python that enables large-scale, fully automatic real-time spike sorting and decoding on hundreds of channels. Our system is cross-platform and works seamlessly with the Open Ephys suite of open-source hardware and software widely used in many neuroscience laboratories worldwide. It also comes with a user-friendly graphical user interface to monitor the cluster quality, spike waveforms and neuronal firing rate. Our platform has comparable accuracy to offline sorters and can achieve an end-to-end sorting latency of around 160 ms for 128-channel signals. It will be useful for research in fundamental neuroscience, closed-loop feedback neuromodulation and brain-computer interfaces.

title: Mapaci: A Real Time e-Health Application to Assist Throat Complaint Patients
authors: J. Bobadilla; P. Gomez; J. I. Godino
venue: Second International Conference on Internet and Web Applications and Services (ICIW'07)
abstract: This paper describes the fundamentals of a complete e-Health Web cooperative information system combining the following features: a research and development platform for telemedicine and patient screening including new voice processing algorithms and a communications framework. The main goals and design decisions, related to architectural analysis of this information system oriented to voice pathology are pointed out. A methodology to handle patients' voice samples, enabling real-time remote capture, transmission, storage and processing is documented. These features allow to define a complete information system including database recruiting as well as cooperative diagnose. Hints on the use of the Java Media Frameworkcopy (JMF) technology and the use of different protocols to implement synchronous services, including audioconferencing and videoconferencing are documented. The preliminary results show the feasibility of the design. Expected benefits are among others an improvement in the knowledge of voice pathology evolution, and the remote screening of large population sectors.

title: An IoT-Based Decision Support System for Real-Time Vehicle Maintenance Scheduling in the Fourth Industrial Revolution
authors: D. Siswanto; A. Farid; G. Priyandoko; N. A. Wahyudi
venue: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) has transformed manufacturing and maintenance through advanced technologies, including the Internet of Things (IoT), cloud computing, and Decision Support Systems (DSS). In vehicle maintenance, IoT enables real-time data collection from Electronic Control Units to facilitate predictive and periodic maintenance, enhancing reliability and efficiency. This study develops an IoT-based DSS for periodic vehicle maintenance, focusing on data from vehicle sensors to optimize maintenance intervals based on mileage and component conditions. The system was designed using a web server and database infrastructure, integrated with Application Programming Interfaces to enable real-time communication between the vehicle's sensors and a web dashboard. The dashboard displays component statuses and provides maintenance recommendations. Testing involved function and performance evaluations on data communication between an OBD-II scanner, IoT gateway, and web dashboard. The system reads real-time vehicle data effectively, provides maintenance recommendations based on pre-set DSS rules, and updates component status on the web interface. Tests confirmed synchronization between sensor readings and displayed data, with a response delay under 500 ms, meeting real-time system criteria. The IoT-based DSS for vehicle maintenance proved effective in automating maintenance scheduling, providing users with timely and accurate recommendations. This system promotes efficient and proactive vehicle maintenance, aligning with 4IR goals by enhancing operational reliability through real-time data integration and automated decision support.

title: Advanced UAVs Hardware-In-The-Loop Simulation Platform for STM32-Based Flight Controllers
authors: I. Laabousse; Y. El Bouzekri El Idrissi; M. Haidoury
venue: 2025 IEEE 8th Congress on Information Science and Technology (CiSt)
abstract: The reliability of control algorithms for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is a critical step in the development process, especially when transitioning from simulation to real implementation. Software-In-The-Loop (SITL) methods, though widely used, often fall short of capturing hardware-specific behaviors such as timing constraints and I/O delays. To address this gap, we introduce a Hardware-In-The-Loop (HITL) simulation platform tailored to STM32-based flight controllers. Our system integrates the X-Plane 12 flight simulator with an STM32F4 Discovery board through a lightweight Python middleware that enables real-time, bidirectional communication. The middleware handles sensor emulation, actuator command translation, and precise loop timing, allowing direct testing of control logic on embedded hardware under realistic flight dynamics. Experimental validation confirms the platform’s ability to maintain stable loop frequencies, low communication latency, and accurate response tracking in closed-loop scenarios. This flexible and cost-effective HITL platform offers a valuable framework for researchers and developers to rigorously evaluate both control algorithms and the performance of embedded STM32-based flight controllers under realistic conditions, without the need for physical flight tests. It significantly reduces development risk and time, particularly in academic and prototype-level UAV applications.

title: Garbage Collection System using IoT for Smart City
authors: M. Badve; A. Chaudhari; P. Davda; V. Bagaria; D. Kalbande
venue: 2020 Fourth International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
abstract: In today's world, one of the major environmental problems is the collection, management and disposal of the garbage. The current process of garbage collection does not consider real-time garbage level in dustbins while generating routes for garbage trucks.
